analysis.name: Ashwin Ramasubramaniam
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor tries to make the course bearable; however, I do not trust him to help be because he said at the beginning of the semester not to use Chegg, AI, or any related outside source, and these outside sources explain calculations to me so much better than humans and textbooks do.

People seem to have mixed feelings about AR but I really think he wants the best for all his students and I am a better engineer because of him. Is the class hard? yes. Is he also fair? yes. If that is a problem I am not sure why you decided to become an engineer.

He is a great guy and I am taking him for other classes so I'll be back to update! Very helpful during office hours. His lectures are kind of boring and a little difficult to keep up with, though he tries his best and is super enthusiastic :) Get help from TAs for homeworks, ask questions, actually do the zybooks and you'll do good!

This is a coding class and half the time he spends in lecture solving integrals. It feels more like I am taking two calc classes. He always front loads the beginning of the semester with all of our text books readings. About 2 or 3 readings a week and each takes about 2 hours if you actually want to learn anything.

This class is heavily frontloaded towards the beginning of the semester. The ZyBooks are tedious, but as time goes on the homework assignments and mini projects are a fun challenge. Prof R. was very helpful during office hours and offered tons of extra credit. He is an enthusiastic lecturer.

analysis.name: Adrian Staub
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst part about this class is the homeworks - they are extremely time consuming but not necessarily hard. Staub is a pretty good professor. He does his best to make lecture interesting and will clarify information if you ask for help. No textbook required. Go to lecture (and pay attention) and you'll get an A

First year that the professor decided to have in-person exams and it shows in the class average. All of my friends consistently do poorly on homeworks and have gotten 50s on exams. Class is poorly structured and grading is harsher than necessary for an introductory statistics class.

Genuinely a great professor. This course can be difficult and surprising because a lot of psych majors seem to be a little wary of coding. However, all the instructions are clear and Prof Staub is a great teacher. If you put away some of the anti math bias, the course material is very interesting and helpful.

Adrian is an amazing teacher and I honestly learned more in this class than I did in any other. He uses R for the HWs (there is one HW for each Unit) and that saves you a great deal of effort in calculating complex statistical problems. The TAs are super helpful in guiding you through the homeworks and teaching you R. Overall a great class and prof

He is a good lecturer. I hate math and didn't understand most things, so having friends in the class really helped me. Exams are online open-note and there are HW assignments through a coding system called R (it's scary at first but alright). The discussion section attendance is optional. Overall easy but not my favorite.

analysis.name: Ysaaca Axelrod
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good professor, kind, lectures are interesting. Will ask you to turn and talk to your neighbors very often, and the final has a group project involved. Cheat sheet allowed on midterm, weekly short quizzes, not a lot of readings or videos. Attendance mandatory though.
engaging lectures and she cares about the subject - a class i look forward too (rare)

Professor Axelrod was by far one of my favorite professors so far. She is so passionate about teaching and her research and always tries to engage the class, even through its abut 80 students. She has very clear grading and is always willing to help. Shes super sweet. Only thing is the exams were harder than expected.
Ysaaca Axelrod gave every student a chance to shine but her expectations for tests were somewhat unclear and it wasn't easy to guess what would be on essays for exams.

Axelrod actually cares about her subject and that students learn the material. Attendance in mandatory, but all quizzes and exams are open notes and online so you should do well. There is also no final and instead a group project. Classes usually end early too. Overall great class and an easy A.

analysis.name: Amanda Raimer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pick anyone but her, please. Practice problem grading is unfair, piles of homework to do every week, and passive aggressiveness at every question you ask her. I remember asking her a question after class and her snapping at me and instead I went to my past biology professor instead. If you want to pass, just take another professor.

Have you ever wanted to meet Helen Keller? If so, take this class and meet her yourself. You will not be seen heard nor will she communicate with you. Always answers questions with sass and annoyance and expects you to grasp the content day one. Lectures too brief yet she talks so fast. Theres bias for grading with the TAs and I regret this so much

Raimer is an okay person, but when you ask her questions she either seems annoyed or just doesn't help you at all. If you interact with her alot she does become nicer and more approachable. She does not give clear exam study guides just a list of objective, iclicker questions and a couple "practice Problems" you're kind on ur own in this class.

Genuinely pick a religion and start praying. Professor Raimer is genuinely one of the worst bio professors I have ever had. Starting off, she never answers questions properly after class or before class and always gives an attitude almost like it is your fault for asking a question? Doesn't explain concepts properly and always brushes over topics.

I really loved taking this class with Dr. Raimer. You do really need to go to class to be able to keep up with the material. The exams are very straightforward and is based only on concepts in the lecture slides. Going through the lecture slides is the best way to study for her exams. This class was manageable.

analysis.name: Eric Sarfo Amponsah
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 180 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Completely unable to maintain interest in class or explain things. Sets literally impossible quiz times, enforces them with a rigidity that suggests he mostly loves a power trip. Regularly takes days to respond to emails. Has difficulty answering student questions clearly. Sets unclear standards for grading tests and enforces them rigidly

This professor does not care about people in extenuating situations. I tried to get help from him but he rejected every request from me. All other professors offered help and weight adjustment to give me a chance to pass the course. He is the worst professor I have ever met this semester.
He's quite condescending, and also automatically assumes students just want to cheat and get away with things. That will be his default perception if you ask him about anything.

If you have no external issues, no disabilities, then you're fine taking this prof. If you do, then avoid him. Even if you are registered with disability services/ Dean of Students, he won't work with you. He might not even believe you.
If he's your only option, and you're having trouble, you're better off not approaching him and just try to pass.

You will learn nothing from taking Math235 with Eric. I repeat, NOTHING! He weaponizes exams instead of using them to test understanding, and his poor attitude towards teaching is already palpable from the start. Even if you do well, you'll walk away feeling worn out. This guy does NOT deserve a paycheck as he thinks students are beneath him.

analysis.name: Seyram Avle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Seyram is a really nice and caring professor! The class consists of reflexive responses which are in class writing prompts, but she gives you the prompt in advance and lets you use notes for it. There is one in person midterm with multiple choice, true and false, and 2 long responses. And there is a group project due at the end of the semester.
Very genuine person and very passionate about the subjects that she lectures about. Very intelligent and fun to listen to.

The class is tough. There's weekly readings, and you will need to write a 300 word response every single week. The grading is brutal. I never once got full marks on any of my assignments. There is a midterm paper, and a final group project. But if you take the time to really absorb and understand what's being taught, you'll be fine.

Don't take this class if you hate reading. Every week we have to read two readings that are about 40 pages long but they are sooo heavy and hard to understand and you have to write 300-400 words reflecting what you read. I dread it. She's also very strict with grading and isn't very flexible. I don't recommend this class, I wish I never took it.

Seyram is a great professor and I would absolutely recommend her to anyone interested in communication. Weekly readings and 250 word response papers were not bad at all. She is very knowledgeable and encourages in class discussion. Very supportive with final research paper. 100% would take again!

analysis.name: Aaron Rubin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Rubin is fantastic, he doesn't care about exams, he cares you do well and understand the content. He focuses a lot in outside work like projects and problems sets but be'll also allow you to use anything you want to get the answers as long as you cite it. Lectures are interesting and fun and he's just a cool dude. Totally recommend him!

I found that I didn't actually learn anything from him. His entire basis is that failing helps you learn so he's not super helpful if you ask questions. I think in certain settings that's good but his lectures and notes were also pretty vague. He sets up the course so you'll succeed but not so much that you retain. submit by deadlines get an A.

Exams are online and can be corrected for partial credit back. Homeworks are hard but can also be corrected but for full credit back so easy to get 100 on every one. Doesn't do extra credit but it's impossible to fail the class. No final exam but a final project that is pretty time consuming but really just graded on understanding and effort.

Aaron is a fantastic professor, lectures are understandable and to the point, and Aaron himself is a very passionate and down to earth teacher. HWs and exams are self graded, and while they're sometimes long and work heavy, it feels very fair, and the midterm so far has been my best testing experience to date; feel like I'm actually learning stuff!

Very nice guy with a clear passion. Makes the class basically impossible to fail, while still feeling like I'm learning due to homework and exams being self-graded with corrections. My only complaint is that the final project felt a bit too open-ended.

analysis.name: Alexandra Jesse
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. unless this class is needed for your major I wouldn't take it. 80% of the final grade is exams (4 exams, 1 final), she records lectures but you can't access it unless you have an excused absence (like being sick), and she talks really soft so you can't hear her well. she's sweet as a person but not the greatest professorl

Really boring class and lectures are really dry. You have to pay very good attention in class and when reading the book if you want to do well. Crutches are there to help (drop the lowest test grade.. etc) but still tests and in class writing assignments are really tough. Definitely need to drop the lowest grades and do all SONA extra credit.

Avoid this prof is possible! Writes her own exams (1st language isn't english), so some questions are confusing. Attendance is mandatory, only get 2 absences. After 1st exam every ~5th class is another exam. Doesn't show final grade on canvas, so no idea how screwed I am. Nice person but not good prof. Avoid, avoid, avoid!!!!

Dr. Jesse is one of the best professors I've had here! The class has no HW and is graded by 4 in class multiple choice tests, a final, and attendance. She's super kind and understanding, and her lectures are interesting. You have to study for the tests, but as long as you dedicate time, you'll do well.

Has 4 exams, including final, drops one of three lowest exams all graded 20% of your grade. If you honestly do well in the first 3 you dont have to worry too much on the final since they are all graded the same. Loved her little accent especially when she says PLUE instead of BLUE. You will do fine if you are passionate about the subject.

analysis.name: Jenafer Andren
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Jenafer is a great professor and super flexible. The lab is 5 hours long with a 45 min lecture which is a bit long especially if you have been a server before. The homework isn't bad and the exams are easy if you go to class
She is a sweetheart and very passionate about her work. She will help you with anything you need outside of class and she is always accessible by email. I highly recommend you take her class.

Jenafer is a great professor. Easy to work with and always happy to help. Small homework assignments once a week, management project and two exams (midterm and final) are what makes up the grade. Don't bother buying the textbook - can help on tests but I got an 87.5 on the first and a 98 on the second without having it.

This class is a lot of fun. The lecture if pretty useless but the lab is great, all five hours of it. Jenafer is a good teacher and really down to earth. You get a lot of experience and should end up with a good grade.
Jen is awesome. By  far the best professor in the HTM department. She is so helpful and actually enjoys teaching. You will learn so much while having a great time!

analysis.name: Benjamin Bailey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His class is so boring do NOT take it. "Studying everyday talk" may sound interesting, it is not. This class is nothing but him boring you, you talking to your partner about nothing, and doing assignments twice a week.

Such a good professor. He engages the audience and does funny, light-hearted demonstrations. Simple assignments, but exams are all open-response. Attendance is definitely important but you can watch the Echo360 and get away with it. Overall, as someone who loves an engaging class and a passionate professor, this was a great experience!
I disagree with some of the people on here. I think he is whimsy and he makes me laugh every class. Not everyone gets his humor but I do and I recommend. He does cold call though.

On a power trip and refuses to admit he's ever wrong. The professor does nothing but repeat the readings and make you teach yourself as opposed to him teaching. Take it if you want an easy A, but don't expect an enjoyable time.

Professor Bailey's lectures were always entertaining! He does cold call, which I was nervous about because I am shy, but you can always say pass. I'm not sure why people said the essays were graded harshly, as long as you follow the prompt and provide detail, you'll be fine. I would suggest studying for the quizzes as they are all open response.

analysis.name: Robert Bowse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His feedback is alright but he gives so much unnecessary busy work compared to other professors you can take. I would recommend someone else.

I loved this professor, he really helped our class feel more conversational and would ask us questions to help engage in glass. He helped us really think about our professional development and how to excel in the business world. I don't like how the grading system changed though but what can you do. Assignments were very helpful too.

Professor Bowse is a good professor in a very useful class. No exams, just weekly assignments which make up for 80% of your grade. Class is pretty useful in getting you prepared for internships, as you work on resumes/cover letters. Some assignments are longer than others, but nothing too bad. Do the assignments and show up, and you will get an A.

Professor Bowse has quite a deceptive rating of 4.3. His grading is extremely picky and assignments must be completed HIS way or no way. In terms of workload, this Junior year writing class has considerably more work than other professors.

The class has WAYYYY too much work for a 1 credit course. To add insult to injury the work is graded obscenely harshly. If you are able to take this class with anyone else do it. In terms of how he actually is as a professor he's actually not bad, very clear and engaging, just assigns way too much work.

analysis.name: Lori Astheimer Best
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 159 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Honestly Lori is best professor I have had thus far. She makes seemingly tough concepts so easy to understand, and gives 5 easy exams with a cheat sheet allowed. Not a lot of work outside class. So many opportunities for extra credit, including an optional discussion once a week which is super easy and helpful. Love Lori and this class!

Honestly just a really great professor. Very clear and informative lectures. Its clear she cares about her students doing well. It is a very content heavy class with very difficult concepts. Also exam heavy, 5 midterms, optional final. Although this class was hard Dr. A had lots of extra credit, and lots of help opportunities.

there are not a lot of assignments to help you if you dont do well on the 5 exams we have. she talks so fast, the only plus is that you can do the class on zoom. The exams were kinda hard and i would not recommending taking this if you are a normal psych student.

Truly the best professor I've ever been blessed to have. PLEASE attend the most lectures you can because they are the most comprehensive and engaging hours of my college experience so far. She has so much extra credit that it is hard to not get an A in this class. Attendance is through TopHat and you can join from zoom if needed, but go in person!!

She is amazing. Dr. A offers a zoom link to watch class live while not attending in person. Quizzes are take home and multiple choice. She is very passionate about neuroscience. The class is very big but she does encourage participation and talking with people near you. She is amazing, even if science is not your thing you can do great.

analysis.name: Paul Bourgeois
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't believe him if he tells you 'it's not true that you have to learn everything by yourself'. IT IS! He hardly lecture anything but to ask your group to do question on the board. Quiz on the beginning of units with actual calculation problems which are completely self-taught . Ok if you have good teammate. Finally TeamBaseLearning is the WORST.

this was a team based learning class. luckily my team was good, but if you end up in a bad team then it will be a terrible class. be prepared to figure things out on your own - people are there to help but mostly it felt like i was teaching myself

The way the class is set up is that you pretty much have to go to class but you won't learn anything because he doesn't teach The practice exams are useless for than actual exam because they are always way easier. I'm beyond upset with this class and hope he gets fired and yes I got an A in the class it was just ridiculous I am also a physics majo

This class was the worst I've taken at UMass. The TBL format is not conducive to learning and Paul doesn't teach anything ever. The only way you will learn is if you watch the YouTube videos he posts and even then you won't be prepared for the exams. The review sessions help sometimes but he structures the exams to be on material you've never seen.

Probably one of the easiest classes I have taken, just applied myself a day before the exams and got 110% on both. the exams are 12 multiple choice (which are pretty straightforward) and only your best 10 count and anything over that is a bonus 10%. Would recommend even though a lot of people dont like the team oriented learning that goes on

analysis.name: Kathleen Brown-Perez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Kathleen is literally one of the best professors I've ever had. To pass, all you really need to do is show up and participate in the discussions. She even bought our class donuts. I highly recommend her and respect her as a professor.

Great professor with a love for teaching and the course material. She was an excellent instructor to have for my first semester of college. Her course was mostly rooted in group discussion. One of the few instructors for 201H that does not require you to buy any materials. I wish I could have her again.

Kathleen is a great professor for Criminal Law. I took this class as an elective and was a little nervous about its difficulty going into it but as long as you care and are willing to put a little effort in, no one should have a problem getting a good grade. This class is at 8:30 and I have no problem getting up for it because its so interesting!

I think her classes are very chill and enjoyable. The content of this course is helpful beyond college life, and she's a nice professor, too. I'd recommend reading the material (she doesn't assign much) and trying to participate in class discussions. Fair grading with clear criteria, you will do well as long as you care.

If you can, take her class for Ideas that Change the World! It's almost completely discussion-based, so attendance and participation are critical. There are 3 graded reflection essays that are super manageable. Getting an A is easy if you just attend class.

analysis.name: Hari Balasubramanian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are really hard to follow. He heavily relies on the textbook and can't explain the content on his own, as he "haven't taught the class in 10 years". His completion and assignments homework are all from the textbook and are 5x harder than what you learn in class. Would not recommend taking Hari, basically taught myself the whole course.

A nice and caring person but not a good professor. His slides are just copy paste from the textbook, he takes all class to give you the one equation that you needed all along and it's very confusing. Instead he takes forever with theory and context. He'll do daily quizzes call that his “attendance”. Be ready for a lot of work outside class

One Of Umass engineering's best professors. One of the first professors i have had who has inspired me to apply my learning to real life problems and other applications.  Many time consuming projects throughout semester, however grades are based upon effort and doing your best to find a creative solution to a problem, often using code.

Really like his teaching style, I normally never go to lectures because the professors are so hard to follow, but I can actually follow what is happening in class. Very nice guy who is accessible outside of class. Lectures are pretty engaging
Highly highly recommend Professor Hari. He was really the first professo

analysis.name: Katie Beltaire
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I love KB, genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. Super passionate about what she teaches and takes the time to learn the names of students & hear their feedback or contributions to discussions. Exams are memorization heavy, make flashcards for the sections of lecture slides written in red/highlighted. Labs are super fun and engaging

Probably the best professor you could have at UMass. She really loves the topics she teaches about, and it shows during lectures. I was never bored during lectures, and the labs are engaging and fun most of the time. The only downside is that she mainly teaches about livestock, which may not be a downside to others!

Dr. Beltaire is very passionate about what she teaches, having lectures filled with personal experiences tied to the slides. All of the information is as straight forward as possible-- you're tested on just what comes off of the slides. After finishing this course, I am very inspired to continue learning on my Animal Science/Pre-vet major track.

Dr. Beltaire is hands down on the of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were engaging and very interesting. She's very passionate and knowledgeable and easy to talk to. Go to class and the labs! It does make a difference in your grade and understanding the material. Don't bother with the textbook, we never used it even once.

She is an amazing person. She is very caring and inspiring. You can tell she really loves what she does and wants her students to succeed. If you have any questions, she is extremely easy to talk to. Her tests were not hard, but there was a good amount of memorization. If you stay on top of things, you will do really well in her class.

analysis.name: Cynthia Barstow
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took Professor Barstow's Advertising and Promotional course this spring and I loved it! She is a creative spirit and has a true and clear passion for what she does, which is refreshing in an undergrad professor. A lot of the class is based in creativity, but she gives deep and specific feedback to help improve. I loved this class!

Everyone should take one of Cynthia's classes!!!! She is a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about everything she teaches. She makes every class feel comfortable and is so friendly to each student. Also the projects are not super challenging, but feel very useful and rewarding. Love her, love her classes.

Gave assignments with no submission on the class platform, over break, and graded harshly with zero feedback. After saying that she's an easy grader and just wants to see effort. Seriously? I had an easier time in Corporate Finance.
Doesn't explain rubrics or what she wants to see. I wouldn't be surprised if she graded on if she liked you or not.

Advertising & Promotion became one of my favorite classes thanks to Professor Barstow. She's incredibly knowledgeable, on top of marketing trends, encourages AI use, and truly cares about her students. No textbooks either, just real & authentic content! No textbooks & a lot of real world examples. I couldn't recommend her classes enough!

She is very good at what she does and keeps her lectures interesting but the class overall is a burden, frankly.  The concepts are so broad and almost common sense but the tests are based on memorization and are very specific.  I went to the lectures just for the iclicker but was on my phone the entire time and still did great.

analysis.name: Kristin Bock
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Bock's class this semester! She always gave insightful feedback on assignments and since it's a workshop class, she would give time to work on the assignments (definitely take advantage of that time). She has a respectful and kind approach to her teaching, but is also very direct which made it easy to follow along!

Prof. Bock is a great instructor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. The course is well-structured, and work is applicable to real-world business communication. She provides fair grading and is approachable if you put in the effort. Highly recommend for anyone looking to improve professional writing and presentation skills.
Professor Bock is super nice and this class isn't bad. It's almost all group projects but the lectures can be boring but sometimes she will let you out early

Kristin Bock is a great professor! She really cares about her students and is very understanding. I have learned a lot in her class and if anyone is looking to take Business Comm I highly recommend her!

Don't know why she has a 4.3 rating. Most useless class at Isenberg and she grades unreasonably hard. The same cover letters and writing style that has gotten me high-level internships was a 80% in this class. Make sure not to use the word "not" or else you'll lose 20 points! Wow I wrote Dear ______ to start a letter. Too bad that was -10 points

analysis.name: Melissa Baker
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Human Resources should not be the most difficult class in an MBA program, but Professor Baker seems determined to make it so. Class requires reading an entire (poorly written) textbook cover to cover, 5 medium-length papers (a.k.a. "exercises"), numerous graded discussions, weekly quizzes on book material, and a very long final paper. Just say no.

Heavy workload with weekly hard deadlines. Read 700 pg text. 11 quizzes-get electronic version of text to help. 5 exercisesmini 2-3 pg papers. Mandatory discussion posts every other week with firm 3 post min and length rules. One 8 pg paper. Limited guidance on exercises. Only interaction with class was feedback on asgmts. Quick but tough grader.

Great personality & lectures. Don't take if you're not an HTM major bc you'll be doing so much work and it's not worth it. The exams are hard, open-response & handwritten. There is a group project you do all semester, but she grades it so harshly. The final grade for the project is not as harsh, but overall, the project is 30+ pages & hard.

The workload was very manageable even if accelerated (6 wks due to summer). There's a mix every week. You have “Exercises” due weekly that are essentially small papers - can be a reflection or training. You get good feedback! My favorite assignments were the self-assessments. I genuinely enjoyed the class and plan to take Professor for HR too.
not sure how I feel about this class. Definitely structured great and her slides are great but lots of assignments and lectures can be boring. Exams are essay questions but not bad

analysis.name: Caroline  Winter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Caroline Winter's class was an exceptional experience for me. After initially feeling unprepared for her class, I took it again a year later and encountered so many opportunities for personal growth. She's detail-oriented, understanding and applies concepts in her teachings to help students become more intentional with their own writing.

Caroline is an incredible professor. Her class is super interesting and easy to keep up with. The readings are long but it's easy to get through them because they're entertaining. She's super helpful with her feedback and always makes sure you're doing okay. 10000% would take again.

Caroline Winters is an absolute gem in the Journalism Department. She's an incredibly talented writer who's published in The New Yorker, GQ, Bloomberg, and every other prestigious magazine you could think of. Despite this, she's humble, caring, and dedicated to helping her students succeed in their writing and in the industry. Take her class.

Professor Winter is the best educator within the Journalism department at UMass. She's incredibly intelligent, engaging and truly cares about her students. The work load is medium, but actually interesting/helpful  (descriptive passages, reading articles, and one big piece on whatever you want at the end). Don't debate it--take it!
The class starts out very reading heavy, but all the texts are beneficial in improving your writing. Caroline is very understanding, and gives a ton of helpful guidance and feedback.

analysis.name: Joe Chiu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 118 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Joe was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures don't offer any help with the difficult exams and overwhelming projects. And anytime you ask for help he comes off as rude and makes you feel stupid for asking any questions. He only knows how to teach people who already know how to code. This class was the worst.

Oftentimes very difficult to understand. I did not find his lectures to be particularly useful or interesting after doing the Zybook, which does a much better job of explaining concepts. He is fairly responsive on Campuswire, but sometimes his responses do not help much with your question.

Firstly, he has a thick accent that makes him hard to understand. Additionally, the recorded videos on Moodle are 480p and lack most info present on the slides, info that's also tested. Lastly, exams are graded out of 40 points, so slight mistakes compound into significant underperformances at the class level. Not the worst, but avoid if possible.

He is absolutely one of the most unforgiving and uncooperative professors I have had the displeasure of having in my lifetime. 

Going to his lectures are the largest waste of time. Even if you could understand the words coming out of his mouth, his methods of explanation and lecture are horrible. 

He NEVER gives extensions. Period. 0 forgiveness.

review_highlights.comment: I get a headache from every single class with him. He just talks at you, nonstop, for 75 minutes. The slides are so full of text you don't know what to look at. When he takes notes, his handwriting is completely illegible. If I get distracted for a second I'm completely lost the rest of class. I don't know how he never learned to make slides right.

The lectures are horrible: cramped slides, head-ache-inducing, hard to follow along, talks too fast and too much, and explanations that are overly complicated, making simple concepts confusing. A few questions on the exam were not covered in class. Once he talked in a British accent and a mob boss accent...the entire class. Head-ache-inducing.

Take this class if you want to waste your time. He talks for the entire class nonstop and uses ridiculous analogies trying to explain things that could have been explained in one bullet point. I don't even use the notes to study and I've learned everything I know from the homework. The slides are so packed with random stuff they hurt your eyes.

Daddy Taffy is an absolute gem—goofy, hilarious, and effortlessly engaging. His lectures are packed with witty humor, playful sex jokes, and a lighthearted approach that keeps students entertained while actually learning. He makes even the driest topics fun, and his warm, charismatic personality creates a welcoming classroom vibe.

Cannot teach for the life of him. Practice problems come out of nowhere and his annotations are incomprehensible due to his horrible handwriting. Takes a complicated course and overcomplicates it through his intricate wording during explanations. Take anyone else if you can please please please.

analysis.name: Martin Elizalde
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easy A Class! Definitely take for your PS requirement! Weekly online assignments/quizzes (2 per week) with answers from textbook or lectures. Online exams all MC and given an 1 hour and 15 mins with 30 ish questions, super easy and you get 2 tries! Online cumulative final exam, super easy! I 100% recommend! The professor is super sweet and nice!

Took for PS Gen Ed. It's clear that Prof. Elizalde is passionate & knowledgeable. He has a great personality, but at times I felt as though assignments & exams were all over the place/confusing/unpredictable despite attending every lecture and studying. This class & the material stressed me out, but I recommend if oceanography is your thing.

Pretty easy class. All of the exams were online and were split to allow you to basically get a 100 on 25% of the exam every time. It's easy to tell that this is the first time he has taught the class, but he tries his best.

Easy class to get an A. The professor was enthusiastic about the material however struggled to explain and teach in a large lecture, making lectures useless. Lectures felt very disorganized because he jumped around slides that he clearly didn't make. Four exams and a final, as well as two weekly quizzes, easy to score well on but can be tedious

Never went to class bc it was a waste of time. Graded on weekly online assignments which are easy, 4 online exams, & an online cumulative final. It's not difficult to get an A, but the exams are wordy/hard to finish w/ the time limit. The lectures were so unhelpful but he posts the lecture slides to use for the exams which you get 2 tries on.

analysis.name: Ehsan Roohi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very accessible outside class (office hours and Discord), lots of example problems done in class. Challenging material at times. The group project was a little chaotic with shipping and printer errors. He's the first professor I ever wrote a review for, really enjoyed teaching us, cares about his students and is super passionate about his material

He's one of the best prof's I've had at Umass. He's incredibly nice, cares about his students, and wants to see them do well. Not sure why he's getting so much hate on here. This was his first semester at Umass and yes some things went wrong/were delayed for our group projects, but it wasn't his fault at all. If you can, 100% take a class with him

There were issues with obtaining the materials to complete the final project as efficiently as possible. However, with current materials, it is still possible, and after all, we are engineers, so it's kind of the point. Besides the project, he is a great lecturer, pretty funny, always accessible on Discord, and certainly cares about his students.

I took this and MIE490A with professor Roohi and he was great for both, I found 490F more interesting but less challenging being an intro course. He is super accessible outside of class and always helpful. Course has a good blend of math, practical knowledge, and a hands on project. I would definitely recommend him and this course in particular.

Prof. Roohi is a great professor and also a really nice guy. He is extremely knowledgeable and able to explain course material with ease, and he clearly cares a lot about what and who he teaches. The course is made up of 20% homework, a group project worth 20%, and two exams worth 30% each. More difficult than 490F but not a super hard elective.

analysis.name: Eleonore Neufeld
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: PHIL100 is a great class. Prof. Neufeld is well-prepared, givs us lots of preparation for essays, and gives funny lectures. She's upbeat and passionate about philosophy. Flurry of negative reviews within the last days seems suspicious, appearing right after an AI audit where some students were penalized for cheating....

I wholeheartedly believe this class was intentionally designed to be ragebait. Lectures are insufferable, homework is glitchy and can make you do 3-4x as much as you're told, she's constantly in a bad mood, explains everything in about as unclear a way as possible, and the discussion sections are actually just tragic.

EN is a fun professor for sure, she definitely likes and knows what shes talking about. The lectures are somewhat interesting but I often found myself on wordle. There are a bunch of annotation homeworks on confusing philosophical readings that honestley make no sense at all. You have to write 3 philosphical papers that also are confusing. Thats it

A lot of reading. Class is more effort than its worth. The lectures are pretty interesting but discussions are a pain to get through. The papers were not graded with feedback and were graded pretty harsh. Take only if you're willing to put in the work and effort you need to get a good grade.
Lectures and a discussion section are required. Lots of reading. BORING lectures but discussions are fine and there is no final

analysis.name: Eric Poehler

review_highlights.comment: Great man and teacher but don't take Roman Civilization. Took it as a GEN ED, turned out to be a struggle. Why? Because besides in class notes, we have nothing to study with! His tests are hard too, random info. With hundreds of years of timespans, it's hard to know what he'll include on exams. He doesn't even offer study guides. Very difficult.

I'm warning you! Do not take Roman Civilization with Eric Poehler. Although he is very nice and passionate, his class will set you up for failure. He offers no study guides for tests, does not help students decipher what is important to know and what isn't, and doesn't post lecture slides on moodle. I get constant C's bc his tests are unpredictable

Roman Civilization w/ Poehler is extremely hard for a number of reasons. The only resources you have are his powerpoint slides and the book. He doesn't hold study sessions, review sessions, he doesn't give out study guides or outlines, and doesn't even post his powerpoint slides on moodle. Combined with the random information he puts on tests, BAD

Professor Poehler is very interested in Roman Civ and he tries to engage students in his lectures. His power points are kind of confusing--its a bunch of random information and you never really know what to study for when he gives tests, his tests have insignificant questions on them. The class was harder than it should have been.

As an art history major I was excited for this class, he is passionate about what he teaches and is respectful to students. The only thing I have to say for this prof is that his lectures and class structure is sloppy. You need to listen to every word he says in order to get a decent grade on one of the 4 quizzes or 3 exams.

analysis.name: Matthew Ferrari
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ferrari is a nice person but his lectures couldn't keep a meth addict awake.  The TA's are the harshest graders I've ever had, and Ferrari does little to combat that despite knowing their expectations are ridiculous.  Took a month to get our first exam grades back.  Really well educated in his field, can't deny that, but the class is miserable

Took Ideas that Change the World with Prof. Ferrari. Super engaging! He keeps things really active with discussions, and I actually got to know my classmates. Didn't love all of the readings, but helps us connect it to our own lives and the real world which keeps it relevant. I also loved his approach to philosophy as a way to live everyday.

Took 201H. He's very big on group discussion and participation, and really tries to get his students to think-- about themselves, life, society, etc. Go to his office hours! He's awesome to talk to, and wants his students to question + reflect on the readings and beyond. He emphasizes keeping a handwritten journal, discourages digital technology.

I'm a freshman and this was one of my favorite classes so far. Visit to Dubois archive and museum were a nice bonus. You read many important texts, and the discussions are interesting. Got tired of talking about technology but it also felt relevant. I was rarely bored. Wasn't into keeping the journal but then it grew on me over time

Loved this class. Ferrari kept us active with different discussion activities and focused on getting us connect readings to our own lives. He's big on small group discussions, so you get to know your class mates. Didn't love all the readings but it moves on to new material quickly. Be warned, no phones and very little laptop use in class though.

analysis.name: Laura Figueroa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Quizzes are extremely challenging with lecture materials not sufficient to score an A on quizzes. Professor grades essays extremely harsh as well. I made the mistake of risking to take this course with a professor with no ratings on this site and will recommend anyone to NOT TAKE this course from this professor to satisfy the biology requirement!

Class was very engaging and fun, the readings were also super short. She does a lot of fun activities and makes it really easy to learn. There were 3 take home exams and 3 writing assignments. Very easy to do well and have fun as long as you take notes and occasionally participate.

Lecture material is interesting but goes through slides way too quickly even though there is a quiz at the end of each class that counts for participation. Exams are 2 hours and are open note but they are not easy so DO NOT BE FOOLED. Tons of material covered but not much homework. (NRC 261)

Took for BS gen ed, attendance is taken via a survey at the end of lectures, so if you really don't want to go you can show up near the end of class. Grades are online exams and a short essay. Offered extra credit through going to a guest lecture as well as a video presentation. Homework before class was to read articles on canvas, not a grade tho.

I loved Laura! Exams were reasonable compared to lectures and the lectures themselves were always engaging and relevant. I appreciated that she took student concerns to heart and changed things in the course to reflect that. I also loved the guest lecturers she invited. New reading per class but nothing was ever too hard/long. Will miss her :(

analysis.name: Michelle Facette
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: She wants you to do well, all tests are open notes, she explains everything so well, not too much detail. Will help you with anything you need. Very little homework, 2/5 classes each section are mandatory.

Dr. Facette is the most straightforward professor I ever had. She has clear guidelines for her exams. If you know the group worksheets, you can guarantee a 90+ on the exam. She also makes plants so interesting. If you put some effort into the class you will do just fine.

Facette taught the second half of this course and was clear with the expectations of what we're supposed to know for exams. Theres 4 exams in total and 6 quizzes (drops 2) that were all online and open book. Your grade is made up of 70% exams and 30% quizzes so be careful not to slip up too much although there were extra credit opportunities.

Professor Facette is very nice and helpful. the class is interesting and she does a good job teaching it. you have to show up for the worksheet days, but they are helpful because they are very similar to the exams which are open note.

Hi love Dr. Facette! She is clearly so passionate about what she does and it makes the students excited about it. If you're at all interested in plant cell bio she's the person to talk to. She's a clear lecturer and takes time to clarify confusing topics. Her portion of BIO335 was manageable and I learned a lot.

analysis.name: Justin Fermann

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS I DONT CARE WHAT YOUR ADVISOR TOLD YOU, THERE IS MATH AND A LOT OF BACKGROUND CHEMISTRY KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED TO DO WELL IN THIS CLASS!!!! Professor Fermann is very knowledgeable and very helpful when you go to his office hours. Take another physical science class if you're only looking to take a gen-ed.

Great professor. practice exams were exactly like the exams, except for the final, which was slightly different. very lenient with homework, accepted late from me many times. lectures were slightly off topic, i had to teach myself sometimes to make it clear. class was enjoyable and engaging. chill guy tbh

Review for 2022

He's an amazing teacher- intelligent, willing to help, and takes feedback from each class to incrementally improve.  His lectures give most of the info needed, and then some interesting info + in-class experiments.  You'll need to teach yourself rarely using the OWL homework.  Four exams, but they're 1/2 solo 1/2 group w/ notes.

You need to go and take notes to do well you will also need to study the text book. Go to class take notes and be engaged and you will do well.

Worst Professor I've ever had. He makes the quizzes and exams so particular and detailed that you look at the paper and say "what am I even looking at." You have so much material to study for yet he chooses the smallest and most random things to test you on

Be ready for the quizzes and exams. It just a midterm and a final. be sure to take GREAT notes during lecture because the quizzes and exams are very specific. You get a cheat sheet so make sure to put as much as you can. Extra credits are VERY helpful so make sure to do the required assignments. 1 group project, read directions carefully.

Professor Fiocchi is a great guy and does seem to care about his students. For some reason though, I am always confused when doing the assignments and exams. Maybe I don't pay enough attention in the lectures but it never seems like I learn much. It might just be me but I've taken 3 classes with Professor Fiocchi and everytime I've struggled. Tough

analysis.name: Robert Feingold
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I had in college. He has the most real world experience of any of the finance professors and it really shows. In terms of work, you will have a couple of projects, a midterm, and final. He clearly outlines what he wants and how to do it. Personally, I did not find this class to be very hard, but I know a few who did.

He is indeed one of the best professors I took. He really cares about his students' improvement in future career. The exam is pretty hard but straightforward but if you pay attention in class you will be fine. There are no recorded lectures and slides are mostly companies' data since it only understandable during lectures. He deserves 5s rating.

Robert Feingold is hands down the best professor I've had through my college career. The topic itself is challenging, but he does a great job breaking down what you need to know. I can't say enough good about him, easy grader, funny guy, easily accessible when you need help, and a caring professor who wants to see his students do well. Love him!

This was a great class to take and Prof. Feingold clearly cares about his students. Exams were hard, but if you genuinely pay attention in class and properly study they will come easy to you. The homework  were relatively straightforward. Group project was not too bad as long as you communicate well with your group.

Robert is a great professor. His class is hard, but he does his best to help you succeed. He gives a decent amount of HW, but its not too difficult and most of it prepares you for real-world work you'll do in the office. His lectures are great. He is entertaining, funny, and gives real world stories from his experiences. His ratings make sense here

analysis.name: Faruk Akkus
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Took his LING 201 class. Prof. Faruk plans his lectures very well, and uses class time effectively. As long as you show up to lectures, you'll do fine. He makes sure students understand the class material really solidly, but won't elaborate beyond the scope of the course. However, this keeps class on-topic and on track.

He tries his best and he's nice, but syntax is very difficult and I think he struggles to explain it sometimes. If you miss a single class, you MUST rewatch the lectures to catch up. It's not a lot of work, but it's a very challenging class and he grades quite harshly sometimes. He's very nice, though, and willing to help those in need.

Great class! Explains the subject matter clearly & is enthusiastic about it too. Communicates well w/ the class & is a good person in general! There's a section where (as it's a gen ed class) we go over the IPA, so if u're alr a LING major & took 201 prior to this, that part'll be pretty easy. If u need to fulfill your HIS gen ed, take this class!

Professor Akkus is very good at explaining difficult concepts. His syntax class is very informative, and I appreciated the detailed explanations on the slides. It is important to show up to lectures, since he moves quickly through the material. Office hours were at accessible times, as were the TA's.
Fantastic at Explaining Concepts. Would take him many times more. This is from 150 Ling not 401 though. It did not give me the option to chose this class.

analysis.name: Steve Fox
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fox was far and away the best professor I had in my freshman year at UMass, he was funny, knowledgeable, engaging, and you got the sense that he really cared about his field and his students. Take this class if you get the chance, even if you are not studying or interested in journalism directly.

Most of the class is pretty straightforward and not terribly difficult. He's a pretty lenient grader and papers aren't terribly long, plus Bull Quizzes (textbook) and midterm is open note. However, the news quizzes were the only hard part as questions range from local national and international news. Theyre either general or very specific questions

News Quizzes can be tough at times, sometimes having rather obscure topics. His lectures are fairly engaging with many real-world examples, and while the discussions can drag a bit, they often do address important topics. The papers are usually fairly straight-forward, with most being a minimum of 500 words. Took for a gen-ed, would recommend.

The class started out with a clear goal in mind. However, as the semester progressed the expectations and the requirements were kind of thrown out the window. I felt that Fox checked out mentally mid way through the semester and didn't really care to give helpful feedback on the majority of work. He makes you question the value of your education.

Took Sports in Film, Literature and Journalism with him. Not my first class with Fox and have always enjoyed them. Aside from a few papers and books to read, the work is not too intense in this class, and he's always flexible about due dates and willing to cooperate with students. Class is heavy on discussions.

analysis.name: Ghazaleh Parvini

review_highlights.comment: Ghazaleh was nice and knowledgeable, but her lectures were sometimes hard to understand. The midterm had an incredibly low average, and wasn't curved.

She's very knowledgeable, kind, and mostly helps when needed, but if you're a beginner, AVOID. She did not seem to know at all how to pace the class or teach to beginners and it made the class terrible for me. Some tests were overly difficult as were all the projects, but the grading policy is very fair. Overall, good prof, bad for novices.

Her time management is a mess. She uses iClicker questions for attendance and gives them out after class has ended, meaning that in order to be marked for attendance you have to stay late. She has also arrived late on multiple occasions, essentially without warning, and it feels like she's constantly in a rush.

She threw a tantrum over a regrade request in which she failed to acknowledge where she was wrong about my solution. She also tends to arrive late to class and lacks overall time management/organizational skills. Apart from that she seems like a nice woman though, and she at least tries (sometimes).

The course felt disorganized at times (e.g., a section lacked an SI leader). The practice midterm was much easier than the actual exam, making expectations unclear. Calculator policies changed multiple times, and students needing accommodations were asked to come to the front during the first quiz, which was uncomfortable.

analysis.name: Matthew Glennon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD! He gives excellent feedback on assignments, emails back quickly, and offers a lot of extra credit. I've never written a review on this app, but people need to know how great of a professor he is!

Professor Glennon was great. Lectures can be boring, but they are informative. He has a lot of guest speakers come in. There are two group project assignments; they are easy if you have a good group and everyone does their portion. There are two exams that are online. There is homework once a week, but it is easy. Great class, definitely take it,

Glennon is an amazing lecturer. He is funny and he keeps class interesting. Attendance is taken at the beginning of class via TopHat and there are three group projects with random people but they are straight forward. Exams are online and all homework is completion.

Matthew Glennon is one of the best professors at UMass. He is passionate about Marketing and does his best to make lectures engaging and interactive. There are 3 main quizzes that are online and easy if you do the homework. I would take this class over and over if I could. He also helped me launch my own soap business.

Prof. Glennon is by far the best professor I've had here at UMass. He cares so much about students and the material he is teaching. He is literally the cutest most wholesome man ever. He brought his dog to class one day - and that tells you everything you need to know about him.

analysis.name: Mike Gentile
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

The readings aren't bad and you have unlimited chances on the quizzes. I would love to have him again as a professor.

Mike is a great professor. His class isn't super difficult and is honestly super interesting. His class is asynchronous on Tuesday and then meets on Thursday. You do have to pay for an online textbook and have weekly textbook readings but honestly this class is SUPER easy. You only have one group project at the end of the semester.

This class was so easy, it was graded by weekly discussion posts, online textbook work, attendance, and a group project in place of a final. He knows a lot about the subject and is very passionate, he takes time to answer student questions at the start of each lecture from the previous class attendance form.

One time, I was driving on campus, and my car broke down. Mike saved me from a burning car and took out the fire himself with his handy-dandy fire extinguisher. This man is always prepared. Then he brought cookies to calm me down.

He made me cry on zoom, called me immature, has been rude to my classmates too. Sends passive aggressive emails. Thinks he knows everything and this program is our lives. Talks down to you. I think he is on the spectrum a little. There are social deficits.

analysis.name: Laura Francis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: Laura is the worst professor I have ever had. She wants students to obtain a greater understanding of biology, yet she doesn't give any tools to do so. I would never take one of her classes again. Exams are all open response and often have random details pulled that she hasn't gone over. Content isn't hard but exams are. Wastes SO much class time.

Her exams are insanely difficult, all open response. 2nd exam average  65%. Quizzes are very tricky out of 20 Q. But you will learn to work harder. Increase your determination. Make sure you are "metacognitively" ready for this class. If you are planning to take this class, I recommend the instant noodle and caffeine dependent starter kit.

I overthought every single question I got wrong on every exam. The questions are worded so poorly and thus do not accurately assess the student's knowledge. 100% open response is ridiculous. Partial credit doesn't help either as the exams are graded ridiculously hard. Good luck... It's a 200 level class Laura chill out

Avoid this class!!! She's super unfair with the students and doesn't curve the overall grade when the class exam average is 60 or below. The class material is fine but boom the exam is super hard and nothing like we are taught in discussions or class.

Professor Francis's class is not meant to be an introductory bio class. Every week there is a weekly 10-12 page problem set per topic, pre-lecture quiz to a set of videos, topic assessment quiz&discussion post. Lectures are i-Clicker questions that review the material you learned from the pre-lecture videos. Exams are all open response.

analysis.name: Jorge Gimeno Robles

Rude when I had to miss class for sickness and classes were fast with little explanation of anything. Same questions with no actual teaching. TA discussion sections are the only reason I did well. The assignments are very easy and clear I will say, the exams not so much. This professor also crossed my boundaries once 😬.

I found this class to be very boring - he used the same slideshow for classes on end, giving the same explanations each time. Couldn't adapt to students' questions. Always looked to TAs for help (admitted they knew more about the grammar than himself). Also rude to many students.

Worst Spanish prof ever. He read off the slides during class. Provided weak examples and hard exams. Your grade is determined on your exams, hw and participation does nothing. Awesome guy, knows a lot about finance. the class is just lecture and a few homework assignments, and exams are online. only complaint is the slides can be confusing and word heavy but super chill class

genuinely my favorite professor ive ever had. took 404 and 402 with him. all assignments are online and does tophat so technically attendance is mandatory but as long as you go to most classes you get full credit. i would go anyway just because class is so chill. TAKE HIM!!

Professor Griffin is the best finance professor I've taken at Isenberg. He is funny, engaging and a very easy grader. No attendance but you'll go just cause he is wicked chill. Hw is every other week w/ lowest grade dropped. One online test and final. Super easy course load and great professor. Every finance major should take 506 and 404 w/ him.

Adam is so energetic and caring. His class is chill and fun.

analysis.name: Jin-Cheng Guu

POLISCI190A

he's helpful and a beautiful spirit. he is one among the trees, and the leaves, the land, and the earth. he recognizes spirit in all God's creatures and shares his love and passion for what Mother Earth kindly shares with us everyday. God Bless Jack Ahern

As a prereq student, it was hard to know what to study. Expected a chill class ended up my most painful one. Found the class unfair with all changes after add/drop she made.

No SI, no resources, no study guides, no help outside class besides only one help session from the TA right before every exam. She flys through hundreds of slides and expects you to know it all. Luckily, the content of this class isn't very hard, but her inability to convey information effectively to students is what made people hate this class.

Professor Caicedo was amazing! She is very passionate about the topic and does a great job expressing that. The lectures are very dense with content and exams contain info from everything (lectures, homework, etc.), but you are allowed a cheat sheet which is very helpful. There are at least 3 extra credit points available which are super helpful.

analysis.name: Andrea Ayvazian
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: The most useless and meaningless course I took. You will learn nothing in her PUBHLTH 160. And course, it is very easy for you to get an A if you can finish all the meaningless and awful journals. By the way, she put many journals due on days during final exam days, which means your review plan for final will be disrupted by this useless course.

Would definitely recommend taking this class. Andrea is an amazing professor and really cares about what she teaches. I found the content to be super interesting and there are no exams or quizzes. There is a good amount of work outside of class but it is mostly busy work and isn't difficult just tedious. 10/10 recommend

This class is super easy. As long as you do the homework and discussion posts, I don't see how you could not get an A. Attendance is very important, so try not to miss class. Prof. A doesn't really do much honestly. As far as I know, the TAs grade everything. Fun class.
Easiest class I have ever taken. However if you value your money and time don't take this class because you learn nothing. No tests, instead you have in class group activities and reflection papers.

such a good gen-ed to take. group based learning so if you get a good table you will be set. just a few assignments a week but none of them take a long time. attendance mandatory but really is not hard to sit through since so many breaks to talk and stuff

analysis.name: Neal Anderson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: HIS section of the course is amazing (lectures + exams). His notes are so detailed and make the content digestible, I just wish he had some example problems in lecture because he and raj were not on the same page. This is one of the only classes were I can confidently say I learned and retained the information in, he's incredible at teaching.

One of the best ECE profs. Lectures can be a bit boring, but he genuinely wants students to succeed. Super approachable, and his office hours helped me clear doubts and go beyond the syllabus. Always greets with a “Hey, how's it going?”—makes him really easy to talk to.
Neal is the best, great guy, I wish he would teach ECE244 instead of raj :(

My favorite professor in UMass ECE. Not my favorite lecture style because he focuses so much on the concepts and I could use more examples, but he's great for advice, remembers students/names, and is the warmest, friendliest engineering prof I've had anywhere. It makes my day better anytime I see him in the hall and he says, "Hey, how's it going?"

Anderson is a great professor. His discussions are better than lecture for 221. He's an expert at clearing up confusion and he does great examples that are relevant to the exams. I found many times that if I was confused by Ciesielski in lecture, Anderson had a way of explaining it in simple terms that made it all click.

analysis.name: Akshay Krishnamurthy
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Homeworks count for nothing and take many hours, lectures go over extremely basic concepts and then we are expected to calculate and prove exponentially harder problems. Exams range from unbelievably easy questions to extremely complex proofs that might as well have been homework questions. He's not ready to be a full-time professor.

It's hard to be mad at this guy cause I think he's actually trying but man is he incompetent. The only reason he could give for taking this class was that it might be useful for interview questions. The homework is very hard and you will not learn much from it. I learned more from the TAs in discussion than in his lectures.

Course was a mess for the most part. Lecture wise, he is no good and often trips up over himself and his lecture slides. Luckily the book and MIT OpenCourseWare exist and make learning on your own very manageable. However, going to office hours, he is clear and concise. Difficult homework and doable exams. Skip the class and learn on your own.

Tests are about 75 percent of the class grade so the homeworks that take many hours don't really count for anything. In the lectures he never solves or understands his own examples well enough to be able to teach algorithms and offered no late days which is brutal because if the homework is one minute late its a zero. Wait for a different professor

Akshay is an ok professor, but I found the Algorithm Design textbook to be more helpful for this class. I struggled with the first third of the material, but by the final I ended up feeling confident with the stuff. Can't recommend taking this class with this professor, but the textbook is good enough to make sure you do alright.

analysis.name: Zlatan  Aksamija

review_highlights.comment: One of the best ECE professors. Charismatic, intelligent. Midterm average was low, 40-50 region. This was expected and intentional for some reason. No clear explanation of how test would be scaled. Dropped the class because of anxiety about grading. Many students get homework answers from Chegg. This class needs a change but nice prof. Don't cheat.

Very nice and funny guy but also a very boring professor. His style of teaching is showing the derivation of stuff through slides with occasional blackboard drawings.  Wished his class was more example problem based. Also doesn't help that the material can easily get confusing. Be prepared to read the book to follow along.

Read the textbook and do practice problems. His lectures are very dry and powerpoint-based when they should be more rooted in examples and problem solving. Midterm was a nightmare then the final was based off the practice exam.

Lab fairly easy. Great lecturer imo
He actually teaches like a normal person idk how to explain it but he swears so much and is so real in the best way possible. Hard class but the way he teaches it is great

This class was a lot more challenging this expected. There was so much information to memorize and just the overall content was not what I was looking forward to. Exams were hard overall and required a lot of studying. Some cool topics and really nice professor maybe just was not for me.
Just don't take any of his classes, does not know how to communicate and his exams and grading are just ridiculous, wouldn't recommend
Same guy here. Also took a picture with him and his fish tanks. 10/10 experience.

he's a smart and is knowledgable. Try to clear your concepts during the office hours. If you do so you're good to go.
First time teaching, great understanding of fundamentals, lectures were kinda hard to follow, and difficult topics were not made easier through lectures
He is nice but the final he wrote was diabolical. Very smart man but forgets that we are not experts like him.

analysis.name: Akiko Okusu
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Akiko single handedly made Bio152 one of my favorite classes. After struggling through Bio151 due to a disagreeable professor and class structure, I was hesitant to complete this course. However, Akiko is attentive, caring, knowledgeable, and compassionate. She is a fair grader and allows some extra credit opportunities. One of the best at UMass.

Professor Okusu is one of the best bio professors at UMass. She cares so much about all of her students succeeding. Her tests are extremely straightforward and 90% comes straight from the study guides she provides. Attendance is mandatory, as she typically asks iclicker questions during every lecture. She allows opportunities for extra credit.

Akiko is overall an awesome professor. She goes through lectures relatively quickly and ends some 30-45 mins early. Only 1 problem set per week with 12-14 multiple choice questions. Only 2 exams, and one final project. Each week, one lecture is content, the other lecture is problem set time. Walks around and checks in with students.

Any negative comments on her are cap, she is by far the best teacher I've had at umass so far. Super interesting professor and an amazing human being. She was insanely supportive of me when I opened up about some of my personal struggles and regularly checked up on me throughout the semester.

Prof. Okusu is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures are interesting and easy to follow, and she prioritizes group work and collaboration in class. She is also very supportive in the laboratory section, as the second half of this course involves an independent research project. She truly wants her students to succeed.

analysis.name: Alejandro Heuck
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class seems a lot more intimidating than it actually is. The problems he covers in class are much more complicated than those on the exams, I used the practice exams and OWL problems to guide my studying and never had issues. His lectures are not helpful for learning the material but if you can do basic math you'll be fine.

I was very scared at the beginning due to the negative reviews, but it the class turned out to be great. He gives a lot of practice exams, which prepare very well for the actual exams. Sometimes the grading in some questions can be a little bit harsh, but not too significant. Average exam scores (70-75ish), will result in an A in the class.

Exams start brutally, but the course as a whole is manageable, and if you can spend a few hours a week to learn to recognise what the questions are asking of you, you'll be fine. Other course activities are very manageable, despite some people's complaints about "tons of work". It's a level 4 class if it matters, but it's not bad!

4 exams, owls, and prelecture quizzes. The lecture doesn't really prepare you for the exams. The exams are difficult.  3 questions exams and you need to complete 2/3. If. you're good at math/physics you'll be okay but if not get ready to struggle.

Professor Heuck is extremely caring and deliberately goes out of his way to help his students attain a fair grade in his class. I found 471 to be very difficult because I've always struggled in terms of physics problem-solving, but he provided grading criteria, aside from exams, which I found to be helpful in terms of understanding the material.

analysis.name: Alex Gerson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: easy but boring (took him for 494LI)

This class has 2 parts, the 1st taught by Gerson. Lectures were dry but if you study the slides & show up it's ok. Everyone didn't bad on his exam so he curved it. He graded summaries easily and if you show up you get 100 in participation. He wants everyone to do good. Ended his section with an A however I didn't like the class bc of the 2nd half.

This semester was a hard one. Our professor ended up dropping out after the first half and Gerson stepped in. He understood the situation that all of us were put in and gave us as much help as he could. He tried his best to clarify and gave us points back when he realized the lectures weren't clear enough on the quiz. Overall a solid, caring guy.

Each week we had to read primary literature and write a summary of it. It wasn't hard, but he didn't give us clear guidelines on what to write. He was also a hard grader and vague with the feedback. Lectures were posted late and always 1 hour long. Careful with his exams. It's a lot of work for the time (75 min for 10 in-depth short answers).

My biggest complaint about him is that he let us out early almost every class.  This was mostly because he would breeze through his lecture slides, without explaining anything.  However he still tested us on the material in depth.  If you prefer to teach yourself the material outside of class, you'll do well.  If you want to be taught, avoid.

analysis.name: April McNally
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
