review_highlights.comment: teaches PubHealth 213/214...so nice! Always interested in her students.  Classes generally small so she really gets to know you.  Show up and do the very few assignments and you'll have yourself an A...it's fun too!

April is really nice. She is concerned when there is anything that u do not get/ do not like. She is young and related a lot with her students. Her TA Steph is THE BOMB!! take the class... 213 AND 214 with her.. its an easy A and interesting stuff

One of my favorite classes at UMass. April relates material to our lives. She is always available to answer questions, gives extra credit, and the material is not boring at all. Great Class and its a lot of fun.
Great teacher. She really cares about her students. She is willing to help if you need it. Readings are pretty boring in 213, but 214 is great. Great class overall. One of my faves.

review_highlights.comment: **this is for pubhlth203** he didn't stay on topic most of the time, would just kind of ramble through while reading directly off of the slides. very rarely did i learn more from going than just reading the slides, but oh well. he's nice so it's hard to dislike him. he's a great researcher who's skills just don't translate to teaching.

***FOR PUBHLTH 203***
Great guy to talk to, genuinely interested in hearing him lecture every time.
Lots of notes to be written.

This class was so confusing. There's no clear grading criteria, and he seems to just come up with stuff for us to do as he goes. Assignments are just busy work, and he assigned a group project with no rubric. Lectures are dull and while he's a nice enough guy, don't waste your time with this class unless you absolutely have to. Textbook used once.

Prof Arku is very nice and the 360 lectures are very clear/interesting/informational. Most of the work is group work so its not that difficult. The class itself is kind of boring and he does sometimes cold call but honestly its not that bad.

HORRIBLE. A lot of small one page papers, a group project, a longer paper and an exam. None of which are explained very well. He just seems to wing it and the class was all over the place. There is only one exam and it is cumulative, and his lectures don't inspire you to come to class so definitely don't take this class with him unless you have to.

analysis.name: Arie Stern
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wanna take a class that makes you rethink your entire major?! Take a class with Arie Stern!!! While yes, he is kinda funny, he has no idea how to teach. His explanations are horrible and he makes simple topics impossible to understand. Things as easy as long division or simplifying fractions seems like brain surgery if you follow his instructions.

Arie definitely doesn't hesitate to make his students feel dumb... also, don't fall for the extra credit for exams... He'll have you in his office for hours explaining all your mistakes and all you will get is 2 additional points. and be prepared to write 500 words per question on the exams and homework.

If you ever have to take this professor, I would recommend dropping out or hiring a therapist because either way, you are likely going to lose your will to live. The lectures feel like riddles that leave you more confused than before, and he teaches as if everyone has an engineering degree. No calculators or reference sheets, save yourself.

Arie does not know how to teach properly. He doesn't have a personality or try to get to know his students at all. Every time he teaches, he explains the material in a very unclear and confusing way. When a student asks a question, he seems mad and disturbed. Does not have a friendly personality and doesn't seem approachable to ask questions.

Given a study guide with material from over the past few units, expected to know every concept but only ten problems get put on the exam. if you do not write as much information as he wants you lose credit. Hard course. Online homework is easy but the TA weekly homeworks are impossible. The class average on every exam was around a 60%.

analysis.name: Arturo Figliola
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely amazing!!! He says hi outside of class, responds to my emails, is very easy to reach and dedicated to helping all of his students. He's genuinely so kind and funny, he makes Italian fun. He teaches by barely speaking English in class, but won't hesitate to clarify. Can't wait to spend the next few years getting my BA with Italian.
Great guy, you have to participate in the class and will definitely learn if you give the effort. Wouldn't call the class easy but studying for the class at least for me was enjoyable.
Professor Figliola is great! He's kind, funny and has an engaging teaching style. I learned so much from this course and genuinely enjoyed going.

Arturo is the best teacher in the Italian department.  It's a shame, though, that he doesn't teach any upper-level courses but 303.  He was amazing.  He explains things in Italian until you understand.  I wish I could have taken him more than once.  He's also nice and hilarious.  Yay Arturo!!!

Here is the truth about this guy: He is charming and funny but he does not have a good teaching method. Very few students can learn from his "emersion method"(no english in the class). It seems like he writes the tests last minute (his reviews are a joke). Dont take this class unless you already have a good understanding of the italian lang.

analysis.name: Christian Appy
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Appy's, "The American War in Vietnam" class is amazing and I highly recommend it to all students interested in taking their History Gen. Ed. The class has three books to read (one written by the Prof. himself), two ID term quizzes, and two essays, and a Final Exam. If you want a very knowledgeable History Prof. then this class is for you!

Appy is a very good lecturer and is definitely very knowledgeable. I am not a huge history person myself but ended up enjoying his lecturers because he made them interesting. His exams were difficult but he let you know about some topics that would appear on them beforehand. His papers were fair and he also canceled our final, which was nice.

I hardly ever say this, but Professor Appy's lectures truly were a delight to attend, even if they were at 9:05 in the morning! He was engaging, always willing to take questions and very well-versed with the content of the course. I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Appy's teaching of HIST201, and would recommend it to anyone interested in History.

Good professor but not a good gen ed class. Attendance policy is the strictest I've seen, if u miss more then 4 classes you can't get higher then a B, 5 for a C ect. These numbers are halved for discussion. Professor Abby interacts little with class making lectures dull and dry. If 9 ams don't scare you then 154 is an very easy DU HS, if not, Run.

He is a wonderful professor. cares about his work (a lot of the readings are his own work -- but good). Very, very interesting topic. I did not know much about the Vietnam War, and now I want to continue learning more. He is also very interested in the lecture; would take it again. GO TO CLASS, PAY ATTENTION!!! Do this, and u will do great.

analysis.name: Arindam Bhattacharyya
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: Haven't gotten my final grade, but I expect an A. He was a good professor, gave group quizzes for attendance credit, and held office hours in case you had any additional last minute questions before exams. Was pretty funny, made some memorable math jokes I may use in the future. Be prepared to do homework though, but he gives extensions if asked.

Showed up to class prepared and was easily accessible via email and office hours. Very understanding about granting homework extensions. Gave group participation quizzes, but nothing too difficult. Just go to class, and you will do fine. Would take calc 2 with him if he was teaching it next semester.

Best professor I had this year. His lectures were enjoyable and made me want to attend. I had to work hard for the good grade, but he made it seem like an achievable goal! Wish he were teaching calc two next semester. Highly recommend if he is still teaching.

I enjoyed attending his lectures, he does a great job at including real world applications to concepts. He is very understanding about homework extensions, I would take more classes with him if he were teaching.
Often unclear in lectures. Balanced out by him being chill with homework extensions, which there's a lot of long homework, and in class. didn't need to do much in class except show up for quizzes

Santiago was a great professor, especially given the fact that this was his first semester teaching. However, this course is incredibly hard. His teaching is good, but do not miss lectures, and even if you don't you will definitely need to supplement your learning with a good amount of studying.
best professor in the math department

Not bad class for freshmen year
Good for an introductory course

review_highlights.comment: This review is for ANIMLSCI 386 Veterinary Oncology Lab. Professor Arcaro is a very good professor and will help you learn an incredible amount of essential lab skills in this class. She is extremely kind, helpful, and smart. Labs are long and packed with wet lab work but very engaging.

You need to attend all classes. Arcaro comes off as a sweetheart but she is not very reasonable or down to earth. Notes aren't easy to take in her class because she moves through slides ridiculously fast. I would have probably failed this class if I didnt read the book thoroughly because I learned more from the book than class lectures.

READ THE BOOK! if you end up in one of her classes make sure you read the book thoroughly, she moves through the lecture notes way too fast to be able to get anything from them. she doesnt do a good job of answering questions during class. her tests are not too hard if you read the book and get all of the key points.

Prof. Arcaro covers a huge amount of material, adds lots of new case studies not in the text.  Great intro to ecology field, beyond high school level because you have to think, read scientific papers, understand problems. You won't do well if you're not interested and expect an easy A and can't handle the fast pace.
I found her lectures interesting.  But the lectures compliment the text, not replaces it.  It is best to read the material before class and use the lecture to reinforce what you read.

The class had nothing to do with landscape architecture and she was incredibly rude to several students. I would like to say she offered constructive criticism but it was just pure criticism she did not help to improve project ideas, just laughed at them.

she was very sweet and funny, but also could be quite rude/dismissive of the undergraduate students in the class. her grading was extremely unclear. the topics and projects were really interested. she's very much more of an artist then a practical landscape architect.
Professor Aragon is super sweet and helpful! This class was a lot of work, but I learned so much, and she always gave great feedback. I would definitely recommend taking her classes.
Carolina is the best!! She is super helpful and understanding especially during covid. taking another class with her next semester.

analysis.name: Lynette Arnold
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great class, but showed visible annoyance when students would be quiet. TA's lead discussion sections, so this is a three day a week class. My discussion section was a bit boring, and the assignments assigned and due in discussion were very rushed and under explained.

Dr. Arnold is by far the most outright supportive of students with accommodations that I've ever seen, and that is the first takeaway I had from her class. Her grading system is incredibly forgiving and makes it difficult for anyone who does the work to come away with a bad grade, and the way she discusses topics is highly engaging.

Not the easiest gen-ed you could take, but the material is really interesting. The iClicker questions in class are often open-response, which is a bit different. The course is split up so that the first half of the semester you are learning concepts, and the second half you mostly apply those concepts. The TAs are amazing in discussion sections

Don't take this class. It sounds interesting but it's not- it's all concepts people already know and Lynette requires an absurd amount of busy work. There's constant writing and heavy readings and it's a just a huge force. Also, several group projects that she throws at you and assumes everyone can work on her schedule. She's very opinionated

At the end of the semester professor drops my grade from an A- to a C- instantly. There was an essay that was due at the end of the semester and I got around an 85 on the rough draft. I sent a final draft that was nearly identical and apparently "looked to me as if it was written for another class". Makes zero sense and she refused to change grade.

analysis.name: Ashish Kulkarni
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Immuno was a fantastic class, and Prof. Kulkarni did shine in this class. The first part of the class was a crash course on the immune system, and the rest was reading and discussing different RP about methods and tools in immunoeg. No HW, one exam, and just some group work that made the class more engaging.

 A class that everyone should consider!

Professor Kulkarni really cares about his students and wants them to learn. This is an engineering course, so it is difficult and moves relatively fast, but if you pay attention in lectures and do the homework you will do fine in the class. Readings are helpful too, especially if you don't have a strong bio background prior to the class.

Prof. Kulkarni is great. His class is difficult but he makes every effort to help you learn the material. He really cares about his students and wants them to learn. He is always willing to answer our questions. His exams are harder but if you understand the homework and attend discussion sessions, you can do well.

Savage, absolute unit of a Professor. Basically teaches you AP bio and math at the same time. Exams are hard but if you take well-organized notes, you too can understand Okazaki fragments. Very approachable, kind-hearted Professor that wants you to be the best chemical engineer you can be. I N S P I R A T I O N A L

Professor Kulkarni is very chill and cares about his students. His lectures are really great and I would recommend not to miss these as the concepts covered are a bit difficult to understand on your own. He has a clear grading criteria and the homework aren't that hard. Make sure to organize your notes for your open-book exam as you won't have time

analysis.name: Ashley Woodman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: LOVE Ashley! She's a fun and meaningful professor, and she does a great job at providing a well rounded introduction to the topic. The class is basically only made up of readings and discussions each week, with 3 exams and 1 group project. There are readings every week, but they're all really engaging and enjoyable.

Great professor. Very quick response and always willing to help with assignments and course materials. Materials were very informative, engaging, and diverse. All exams open notes and quizzes are based on student generated questions. No text book and novels that were required were very short, easy and enjoyable also. Highly recommend this professor

Ashley was an outstanding instructor and created a safe and inspiring learning environment. Each reading and assignment seemed carefully chosen and contributed to my learning. Ashley was very accessible outside of class and demonstrated deep care and concern for students. She also offered assignments in multiple formats to ensure accessibility.

While I think what Professor Woodman is doing with DDHS program is great, she should NOT be running it. She is EXTREMELY disorganized. She never gets backs to emails and is always behind in grading. During the last week of the semester, we only had 2 out of the 6 papers graded. Having her as a professor is extremely frustrating and stressful.

Psych481 was a very interesting class and Ashley did a great job teaching it. The class is mainly just group discussion about different topics and readings. There is no real work outside of class besides a few readings and a final project/paper. I loved learning about the impact of disabilities on families and she brought in many speakers.

You are graded on are R labs that he doesn't give clear directions to. He gave feedback to fix the labs and even after the corrections, said more was wrong but it was too late to fix it

Class is centered around reading primary literature, although the environment isn't always so great for productive discussions. Getting your genome sequenced is a fun extra to this easy A course.

analysis.name: Michael Blomfield
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I'm on the fence about Blomfield. On one hand, he gives good feedback and is pretty accessible outside of class, but I think he's also a bit of a harsh grader. Capsim takes over the second portion of this class, so beware of that. Make sure you know what you're doing on the simulation or you won't do good on the final. No exams other than the final

this mans voice will make you want to die. you wont think so at first, but wait for it. going to his OVER AN HOUR LONG LECTURE feels like there is broken glass in my ear drums and my face is melting. 
other than that, super easy class. you will probs get an a if you study for exams. (he is bad with technology and goes over class time)

Lectures can be boring because he's not the best at making things interesting, but his slides are well made and you can learn a lot from reading off them. Quizzes are sometimes difficult, but they prepare you well for the exams which are not hard IMO. Group project was relatively easy too. The class was great!

This review is for Management 494BI Capism's capstone course. I disagree with the ratings, yes his lectures are boring to listen to for sure. But he's smart, he gives good feedback, he's a fair grader, he embraces students who require help, overall take him for sure.

This prof will bore you to death, but the class is interesting. On the first day you will probably like his British accent, but by the end of the semester you will want to cry. The exams make up a lot of your final grade, but he provides an in-depth study guide. There are 2 group projects that you do not get to pick your partners (graded easily)!

analysis.name: Scott Blinder
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Blinder is a decent professor who gives you the information very clearly with very little fluff around it. He's basically the type of guy you'd think of when you imagine a college professor. This course is EXTREMELY back-heavy, 65% of your grade is decided within the last 3 weeks of the course! He also posts his powerpoints on moodle!

Scott is a nice guy, but he was easily the most unorganized professor I've had at UMass. Most grades were in the last 2 weeks of the semester, and they were graded incredibly harshly. Very unclear, gave me a grade that did not represent the rubric, with unclear feedback. We did not know what to do most of the time, and neither did he. Bad class.

Blinder is a nice guy but he was all over the place this semester. His grading criteria is very unclear and gives little grace while grading. His use of lecture time was often times misused to talk about news for the entirety of class and to top it off he made us watch recorded lectures on our own time. Sorry to say this was one of the worst classe

Professor Blinder is a gem. There was an exam at the beginning of the semester which was easy if you studied. There is one group project but he does ensure there aren't any free riders on the project by having students give feedback on the students' work in the group. He also welcomes participation and is genuinely extremely caring about students.

analysis.name: Lee Blackstone
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class was my favorite one I have taken. While the reading load may be substantial, every book is captivating, and his feedback is active/supportive. The lectures are informative and interesting, making learning enjoyable. Don't hesitate to take this class with Professor Blackstone!!

Professor Blackstone was the absolute best professor that I have ever had!!!!! He genuinely cares about his students and actively participates in the class. Readings were fascinating!! Whatever your major is you will learn things in this class that you will never forget. You will also learn a lot about yourself! He is genuinely a very nice person!!

One of the best professors I have at UMass. You can tell that he is genuinely interested in helping students learn the material. There's a decent amount of work, but read the lectures and you'll sail through the class. Would definitely take again.

Assigned many discussions but not to the point where it was unmanageable. The only thing I didnt like was that they were due on fridays and that we had to respond to a classmate on EVERY post which can be difficult if you are the first one responding because you have to go back.

I absolutely loved SOC 242 with professor Blackstone. The class a lot of reading and will keep you busy! The lectures are interesting though and the topics really make you think and teach you something new! He gives excellent feedback and generally wants everyone to succeed. Its not a class you can slack through but definitely worth taking.!

analysis.name: Guy Blaylock
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: do not take this class if you're looking for an easy PS gen ed. It doesn't matter if there is no lab attached to this class, do nottttt take it. exams are worth over 50% of your final grade. so it doesn't matter how well u do on the thousands of hw assignments, u do badly on the exams, u FAIL. And the cherry on top is the exams are short and HARD.

Failed this class the first time around and had to retake it a year later. My favorite course both times. Blaylock has the driest sense of humor and never laughs at his own  jokes. Worked with leaders in his field yet doesn't take himself too seriously. Just go to the homework helps and office hours, submit hrw on time and you'll get an A

Blaylock's got a good way of teaching the course and explaining such difficult concepts (his lectures and demonstrations are great). He's helpful outside of class (pro tip: go to the homework sections) and it's clear that he wants you to pass. I'm not a science person, and while this course was a lot of work, I really enjoyed it.

Professor Blaylock is an amazing and funny human being, but with that being said, his class was the opposite of amazing. Professor's sense of humour was the only thing making the lectures bearable at all. The homework assignments while weekly, were insanely difficult and didn't have to do with material covered in class at all.

If I could give Guy a zero I would. Lectures were mediocre at best and cringy at worst. Homeworks are worth 45% of the grade and are long, difficult and graded harshly. Two exams make up 50% of the overall grade and are trivial MC questions that are difficult to study for. The exams do not relate to the class material at all and prof isnt helpful.

analysis.name: Michael Bloomfield
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super boring lectures no one would go to class and just take the tophat in their dorm. Exams have companies from lectures and the questions are worded very strange. He is so unbelievably boring to listen to and waking up to hear him yap for over an hour at 8 am is brutal. The group projects aren't hard if you have a good group, just time consuming

Super long lectures with huge slides. Attendance is required, but you can do an assignment online to get the participation points. Have to do 2 group projects that are 6ish page reports. The exams aren't too bad, but the wording can be a bit strange. Have to make sure you know the examples he provides in class, as they'll appear on the exam.

Lectures were boring but he would take attendance. Exam 1 was harder than 2 and 3, make sure to study everything and also the companies that he talks about during lecture. Although the material was easy, the exams were worded to be confusing. There are 2 reports and you must work in groups.

Yes the lectures can be boring, but it's an easy class and I learned a lot and found the material to be interesting. 3 exams and 2 group projects, both are easy. He cares about the class and students and is willing to help. Slides are posted before class, look through them and take notes so you can pay attention in class - the slides are lengthy.

Pretty easy class but 3 tests make up for around 50%+ of your grade. Tests are simple as long as you study the study guide and watch the videos for recap. Professor gives you time to make up attendance every week incase you do miss class. No extra credit so every point matters for this class.

analysis.name: Danielle Blackman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The grading was based on completion, and i never missed any points for assignments. Good teacher and good prompts, i definitely improved my writing over the course of the class

Dani is hands down one of the best english teachers i have ever had!  She brings a whole new view to writing that i have never gotten before and really helps you to develop your own unique writing style.  Even if you dont like to write, you will like this class!

Danielle is an awesome professor.  She actually got me interested in writing where as before I basically hated it.  The way she teachers her writing class is unique in that students can truly express themselves through their writing.  Highly recomdended.

Danielle Blackman is an awesome teacher. She is very understanding and knows how to teach English well. English is not my first language and I still got a 4.0 in her class. Attend class daily, put time into your papers , and you will get your 4.0!
Words can't describe this class.  We have an awesome time together, and I wish we could keep taking this class into the future.  Awesome, Awesome time.

analysis.name: John Blickford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: John is kind and funny, and he doesn't make things overly difficult or complicated. 4 exams, and you get two chances to do a makeup exam if you aren't happy with your grade. He does surprise reaction papers during class but there are 9 total and I think only 4 or 5 are necessary, so if you miss class one day you should be okay.

Bickford was great! Sometimes his class was a little dull but I could always follow what he was saying. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, take it. His tests are open note and the grades aren't just based on tests which is always good for getting a better grade.

Bickford is engaging, funny, and makes class enjoyable. You do something interactive every class, including PRS and Reaction Worksheets you need to pass in, which count towards your grade. It's a fun psych class, & he allows cheat sheets on all exams.
His last name is Bickford so i think there was a typo but he is overall a great professor. I have taken two of his classes and his grading criteria is clear and feedback is always given.
best professor ever. he's super engaging with the class and funny. the tests are open note and exactly like the notes and textbook readings.

analysis.name: Semih Boz

review_highlights.comment: So monotone, lectures put me to sleep. But all exams are open notes. He was nice, caring, and understanding but I didn't retain any information from class. He's a great guy that cares about his students. Very flexible and if you reach out to him he is always ready to help. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives pop quizzes like once a week. However, he moves very quickly and is not the best at teaching. Does not slow down for students, kind of goes at his own pace.

Semih is a great guy. Took the class in the spring of 2024; not sure what has changed but he was always easy to reach outside of class and genuinely cared about the students who made a connection with him. He does have pop quizzes and the tests are annoying but overall if you prep for them and ask questions you should be fine.

Great person who is very understanding and cares about his students. Understands that the material is difficult and tries to make it as understandable as possible. Very flexible on homework assignments and tests understands you may need extra help.

analysis.name: Christopher Boone

review_highlights.comment: Class is easy and lectures are good but he talks really fast and doesn't allow laptops. Discussions are the most helpful and what will help you really learn. Super nice guy, talks soooo fast. That man is not on speed, he is speed. But the lectures are posted. Lots of hw but it's not hard, good to raise your grade. Put in the effort and you'll do fine. Prof Boone rlly loves what he teaches lol.

This class was my hardest class so far but that's simply because I have absolutely no background in economics, and took stats instead of calc in high school. Lectures are packed with info and go pretty fast. DO NOT SKIP a lecture if you value your sanity. Discussion classes mandatory, exams scaled, extra credit, lecture heavy, and good teacher.

Boone gives a lot of outside work to do but it's all related to what will be on exams and to help you understand the material or help get you ready for lecture. The weekly problem sets are annoying, but if you do all of them and do all the other homework you will do fine. He curves exams by a lot too.

Boone is a great lecturer, but it can be hard to get a chance to talk to him due to the sheer class size. 
You generally don't need to attend lectures, but he usually explains content better than the study guide's do. 
Your grade is in large part based around your score on exams and a small number of problem sets.

analysis.name: Boone Shear
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

TAs do the majority of the grading.

Love this class!!!!

I honestly didn't enjoy this class very much. Its possible that Anthro just isn't for me, but I found most of the material to be very pedantic and boring, and generally the class felt kind of pointless. Boone is kind and the coursework wasn't too difficult despite this. Weekly journal/response activities, manageable readings, easy final and midterm

analysis.name: Forrest Bowlick

review_highlights.comment: He's a nice guy with a well-structured class. Our assignments are GIS labs where we have multiple TAs to help us. You can turn in things late with no grade-related penalty (not turning in an assignment will block you from accessing the next module, however). Fun final project which is a poster you present at a symposium. Has a snack box in lab.

This class was great - pretty much all of the work for it and most of the learning gets done in lab time which is really well structured and you always have the TAs and Forrest there to help. He's a super fun and caring guy who I'd definitely recommend taking a class with.

Love Forrest, he's really understanding and helpful. I really did not understand GIS but he helps you through it. Lectures are not really important, just have to go to labs and complete the labs (since that's all you're graded on)

Forrest is a really nice guy, and a good teacher. His lectures didn't always seem to relate to the labs, but that's ok. The labs were a lot of work, but the help of the TA's and Forrest made them do-able. Super helpful, and gives plenty of opportunity to earn back any points lost if needed. I went from a 60 to a 90 on an exam with the extra credit!

forrest was a great professor! it was easy to contact him outside of class and labs were graded fairly with opportunities to correct them for some points back. he was a funny professor and cared about his students. 100% recommend taking him for gis!!!

analysis.name: Brian Sargent
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If I see Sargent in hell, I won't even say hi. His class grade is only based on 3 exams with 25-30 questions that are poorly worded and more than one right answer. He does not reply to emails, or care about his students at all. I took this class as a pre med and its harder to score than my toughest science classes.

Not the best gen ed to take if you're looking for an easy A. Grade is based on 3 exams and no extra credit. Exams are only around 30 questions long and some of the questions aren't even based on his lectures! You can't even watch the lectures until you email him and have an excuse. Not a flexible class and doesn't explain lecture materials well.

I would not recommend this class. Quizzes are frequent and full of trick questions. The biggest issue is the group project worth 50% of our grade, assigned halfway through with very vague instructions. asking for help only made it more confusing and made us feel more alone. Overall, it's stressful, unclear, and lacks guidance. Avoid if you can.

goes way too fast in lectures, makes lecture notes extensively long (my hand is cramping as we speak), refuses to posts lecture videos online unless you emailed him you were absent ahead of time (can't rewatch lectures to study for exam), gives no study guide or any help when preparing for exam. 2/10 do not recommend.

Professor Sargent is an excellent, organized teacher. His lectures are super engaging. His course builds practical historical research skills through a semester-long project. Brian is a fair grader who gives personalized feedback, even in a large class, and shows genuine care for students. Highly recommended.

analysis.name: Jeanne Brunner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: Dr.Brunner is a great person and they made the topic fun and engaging. You also get notes on the exams too.

I don't know why people are writing that shes rude and her lectures are boring. It is a very easy class, you don't need the textbook and quizzes are open note. She explains concepts well and has many turn and talks during the lecture so you get to chat and get help from the students around you. This class was easier than AP psych. Great prof!!

She can be mean sometimes but she's not that bad, and the class is not difficult, you don't need the book. Attendence is mandatory, but you have around 4 free absences. The only thing is that her quizes and test are very confusing and 3 out of 4 anwers can easily be correct but only 1 gives you points.

So rude, and showed no respect towards her students. It was difficult to reach her outside of class, because she rarely responded to emails. The class itself wasn't particularly difficult, but because of her attitude HUMDEV270 quickly became one of my least favorite classes. Sitting through her lectures felt like watching paint dry.

Prof Brunner is a really nice person, knew all of our names in a 75 person class. Fun group project. There was an excessive amount of reading, however you could get by just skimming. The quizzes for each chapter were 5 questions each and not hard if you at least skimmed. Attendance is taken at every class meeting and is 5% of your grade.

analysis.name: Steven Brewer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

Don't take this professor unless you hate yourself and love pain and anguish and unclear guidelines and poor instruction

He made us go out in the field and do random studies for the numerous pointless projects in the class. Why was I made to go count the number of lichen on certain trees across campus on several different occasions? In all honesty, this class just gave us inconvenient projects that were more annoying then difficult. He was obsessed with lichen.

Professor Brewer is one of the nicest Professors I have ever had. As others have mentioned, some of his assignments are confusing but if you just shoot him a message he will usually respond to you within minutes to help and explain. He is just a super easy going and nice professor all around! Highly recommend!
this class was a waste of time and his assignments made no sense at all. do not take!

analysis.name: Kathleen Brown

review_highlights.comment: Kathleen runs one of the easiest classes you will take, but there were times when she gave blatantly false or outdated information, and if you have a background in the social sciences, you may notice how she butchers some topics and misses a lot of nuance. I'd love to take her class on American Indian Law, but 201H with her was unfulfilling.
Great professor. She provides all material needed for finishing reading. She is also very kind and caring plus nonchalant.

Kathleen is LITERALLY the BEST professor you will ever find at UMass!!!! She understands that this class isn't meant to dominate your life and so she keeps it fairly simple and gives clear instructions. And everyday at the end of class she offers you help and to go to her office with her. She also gives some extra credit assignments during semester

Class=mandatory, but get out early some days.  The books are interesting and as long as you're trying, shell help you. DO NOT fall asleep or be late.  BUY the MLA handbook and bring it to class. Shes very proud of being native american so dont her started on how the world has tortured her people. Thinks shes the greatest, but its funny so its okay.

I loved Kathleen's class. I strongly feel like an honors requirement like 291A should supplement the curriculum, not overtake your semester, and Kathleen did a great job with it. The reading was light; we had no essays and only one project. You don't have to buy the books; she provides the passages online. Would recommend her for this class.

analysis.name: Brian Baldi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

Be ready to read and participate, but he won't twist your neck on talking in class if you truly do not want to. He's really understanding about everything and really easily accessible if you have any questions.
a smart guy, and a pleasure to work with. he legitimately cares about getting his students engaged with the class and offers a pretty laid back atmosphere in which to work. ask him about asparagus.

Brian is AWESOME, a real gem of a teacher. He's incredibly passionate about English and tries to inspire his students to really think and discuss their thoughts. I stayed back to talk with him many times and he's just an awesome person and is a real nerd when talking about certain books/authors. He also brings cookies to class often!

HE IS THE BEST. He cares so much about his students, is so funny, and wants you to succeed. I cannot say enough great things about Prof. Baldi and I mean it. It is the total truth that this guy is extremely kind, personable, and easy to talk to. The material is easy as well, and you have plenty of time to do it all.

Really genuine guy. Makes the class atmosphere super relaxed and brings snacks to almost every class. The class is pretty straight forward, the work load is fairly low, and he grades super easy (I've gotten good grades on responses written on my walk to class). Highly recommend taking class with him.

analysis.name: Brenna Casey

review_highlights.comment: extremely supportive in helping students construct better writing. im convinced that the reviews stating she is mean are misconstruing her dry sense of humor. she was nothing but respectful toward my class. she does have expectations for class conduct and how assignments should be submitted, but they are reasonable and easy to follow

Arguably one of the worst professors I have ever had. She didn't grade anything throughout the semester, was terrible at clarifying discussion topics in class, and overall had a terrible attitude. She was not funny, not charming, and would belittle students who may not have had the analytical skills she expected. 0/10, will NEVER see her again!

I can see how some students might not like her personality, but I enjoyed her class. Really intelligent professor. Brenna is the best professor I've ever had hands down. She's an absolute legend. I've never felt so inspired to write before, and everything we read for class was amazing. Discussions were so funny but also very thoughtful. If you take her class you're in for a treat, also you should look up some pictures of walt whitman because that will come up:)

Brenna is my favorite teacher at UMass.She is very smart but lectures in a way that helps students understand by simplifying complex history.Every assignment is predictable,she is clear about grading,she gets assignments back to us with extensive notes within two weeks of submitting it, she is flexible with extensions, always open to office hours!

analysis.name: John Bickford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand how some people are honestly complaining that the class was too easy? Do you know how dumb ya'll sound? The man is funny, the content is interesting, and you have to be the biggest bum on the planet to not pass this class! It's like you idiots want to drown in homework and stress over exams

Professor Bickford really cares about making his classes enjoyable for his students. He understands the stress students are under, and he really just cares about teaching on topics he loves. AMAZING. FANTASTIC. WONDERFUL. I LOVE HIM. AMAZING CLASS. 10/10, WOULD TAKE AGAIN.
4 Exams allowed with a cheat sheet each. Homework is pretty easy and the lectures are interesting. Go to class for i clickers and response questions, they aren't hard.

Prof. Bickford is a solid choice for a psych professor. He is very lenient with extra credit and doesn't usually assign a lot of homework. His tests are open note but even then they're not very hard. analysis.name: Erin Butler
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great choice for a CICS305 instructor. Professor Butler was a wonderful professor who was very compassionate towards her students and showed high flexibility towards student situations by making herself easy to contact outside office hours and encouraging a judgment-free learning environment in class. Very charismatic, I enjoyed this class a lot.

This woman is a savior for any computer science student who wants to avoid Michelle Trim for 305. If you can take 305 with Professor Butler, please do! Organized course structure, reasonable workload, flexible accessibility outside class and office hours, and welcoming learning environment. I'll take classes with Butler again if I have a chance.

Such a sweet lady!! You can tell Professor Butler genuinely wants her students to be successful and is very easy to contact outside class. She always helps me a lot, and I revise my papers based on her feedback. It works! As long as you put full effort into the papers and participate consistently, she will know. And your grade can be paid off.

She is by far the most humble and down-to-earth professor I have seen in the English department. Prof Butler was always open for deep ethical discussions and never placed a students' view beneath her own's. 
Her feedback for graded assignments is extremely useful. I found it easy to review my work to receive better grades based off her feedback.

It is clear she cares about her students, grading is more than fair, and there is an extremely generous extension policy. Lectures frequently involve discussion and generative writing so you are not sitting and listening for very long at a time, which is good. Definitely take 305 with her.

analysis.name: Brenda Bushouse

prof bushouse is one of the worst profs Ive ever had. guidelines to assignments are never clear, & her lectures are completely disorganized & all over the place. she acts like a high school teacher, looking over students shoulders to see what they're doing on their computer & monitors students in a stalking way in class. highly do not recommend.
.

analysis.name: Christopher Meacham

He seems non-approachable but when I email him he's super helpful and timely. Great course. Learned so much. Not to mention he's hilarious, hilarious, hilarious!

He is an incredible lecturer and super super funny, but the content of the class is really difficult to understand a few weeks in, and it only gets more difficult. There's barely any homework you actually have to do, the grades come from weekly discussion sections where there's one graded question on anything from the lectures, so you gotta lock in

The grades on assignments and tests are quiz based, and graded unfairly harsh for a Gen Ed. It was very frusterating, slides were never used, the writing on the chalkboard was illegible and audio was missing in online lectures.The sound of the chalk scratching the chalkboard and the amount of chalk flying around is also quite annoying.

Funny guy who I think makes the content interesting. Attendance not mandatory for lectures but I recommend going because he writes a lot on board which is hard to see on Echo360. Good amount of reading assigned but I didn't find them too important for getting work done. Only assignments were weekly question in discussion, 4 freebies.

analysis.name: Christopher White
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

The material is difficult enough that you have to study but easy enough to keep up, he's always glad to answer questions and review and clearly enjoys what he does. Also clearly loves bow-ties.

Class says no previous music knowledge required, which is completely untrue. He talks to fast and half of the things he says have no correlation to what is on the quizzes, which we have like twice a week. The class is extremely boring and super hard for no reason. Don't take for gen ed!
He talks too fast and nothing he explains in the class shows up on the absurdly hard exams that happen twice a week.

analysis.name: Maciej Ciesielski

Prof. Ciesielski is incredibly invested in teaching his students, going to his office hours will truly help you understand concepts better. Trying to decipher the notes & textbook alone is impossible so make sure to collaborate with other students and ask questions during class.
One of the worst in Umass, please widthdraw from his class

This class was great! During lecture he sometimes talks about stuff we hadn't learned yet but he's happy to answer any questions and explain, which he does well. His office hours are great, he's a really nice guy. There is an auxiliary textbook but you don't really need it as long as you dedicate time to understanding the homeworks

Homework is usually pretty long and tough, but if you can grasp the homework, you're golden for the exams. Show up, pay attention and study! Just don't expect it to be a walk in the park, it is engineering after all.

Go to office hours, he'll basically guarantee you get 100s on the hw and will also drop hints and tell you whats on the test or not. Make an effort, show that you care, and he'll reciprocate and help since most of the class doesn't do that, shown by the low test scores even thou they're the exact same as the practice. Just my personal experience.

analysis.name: Renee Ciulla
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ciulla doesn't have a teaching style. You have a teaching style. The only teaching done is by yourself. You read and you read then you write and you write. She has the most work to complete and spends the least amount of time teaching.

Ultimately had to withdraw from this class midway through the semester. I wanted to like Renee, she's a nice person and easy to talk to but assigns so much work with hard deadlines to make (7pm on both Thursdays and Sundays every week). Also has a minimum word count on weekly homework (usually at least 450 words). Overall pretty inaccessible class.

Shes so smart and has a lot of experience in Ag which would be so helpful if her homework wasn't so mind-numbingly boring. It is just link upon links of monotonous articles which you then have to regurgitate in at least 300 words minimum. I hate her classes, spare yourself the headache.

Took Sustainable Ag. Renee is super kind, but this may as well have been an online class (boo). All educational components are online blackboard posts and readings. Assignments are long and boring. We visit farms once a week as our only face-to-face time, tours are cool but we end up spend hours doing free labor for the farm more than learning.

Lots of writing but I have taken several of her classes and have always got an A. She expects a lot of effort compared to other courses but marks very fairly. I like her classes because its always the same structure and expectations. If you are literate you can get a good mark in any of her classes.

analysis.name: Scott Civjan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you don't consider Dr. Civjan to be an excellent professor, you are in the wrong major. He is more than fair in his grading and is truly passionate about what he does. He wants you to learn and cares about the success of his students.

terrible grading system, way too much homework and readings, grades exams and homework unfairly, this class alone took up as much time as all my other classes combined (took 5 including strengths), unclear/trick exam questions, spend hours in the library studying, good luck for real ill be praying for you, the only thing is the lectures are good

Best CEE professor! I took class with mixed feelings, and although it was not easy, I loved it! None other class was anywhere near the real-life problems encountered here. He does not let you repeat generic problems, but teaches you creative thinking while doing design/consulting type problems.

The material professor Civjan teaches is far from easy, but I think if anyone else was teaching it I wouldnt do nearly as well. He is really good at explaining the tough material in his lectures. Homeworks are really tough but they are important for understanding the topics.

Dr. Civjan was an amazing professor, he really cared about his students even offering to meet up and set up office hours to help with homework. Pretty flexible with homework deadlines as long as you provided an acceptable reason. Homeworks were pretty lengthy but could easily be done with the manual and lecture notes.

analysis.name: Anne Ciecko
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Does too much for a 200-level class. Self-assessments are annoying and so unnecessary. Asks which dates I was absent from class or was partially there like I remember. Boring lectures, learned nothing in this class. It's like she wants us to treat this class like the most important class for our major when it's not.

I've taken 3 classes with Anne. I liked her at first, but as time passed I found myself dreading her classes. She is disorganized, despite what others say. She childishly ignores her emails. She will never ever ever let you know what sort of grade you have until the end of the semester. She's a one trick pony when it comes to subject matter. Avoid.

I am shocked everyone seems to be grading Professor Ciecko so well. I took Asian Pop Cinema and it was PAINFUL. She would jump from one subject to another, one country to another, and most of us had no idea what we were supposed to have learned. I needed an extension on my final portfolio and I asked a week in advance, she did not respond at all.

Really fair and honest. Great guidance with research and writing, excellent movies. Very knowledgable! Makes material interesting and really cares about student ideas. Provides lots of help and encouragement. If you don't come to class or participate or procrastinate, it will be extra tough, though.

Never grades anything until the final and is extremely selective with grades. Your whole final assessment and midterm is proving to her what grade you should get even though all the assignments can already be found on moodle. Also is ridiculous for deadlines, she will make them at random times noon on a sunday, 12AM on a saturday 5PM on a monday??

analysis.name: Laura Ciolkowski
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor C is probably one of the best professors at UMass, but definitely don't take her class if you're just looking to fulfill some diversity/global Ed requirement - she will make you work for that grade. That being said, if you are at all considering Women's Studies please take 201 with Professor C. She really cares and will teach you so much.

She is no doubt passionate about these subjects. However, majority of the classes are intended to be student led and she is CONSTANTLY disrupting. If she wants to speak the entire time, she should just lead the class as a typical lecture. Her intentions may be true, but the interruptions take away from student participation and seem narcissistic.

Professor C. is one of the most passionate and inspirational professors you will ever have. She give A LOT of dense readings so do not wait until the last minute to read them because they are time consuming and difficult to understand. Do not take for a gen ed requirement and you have to be interested in WGSS otherwise you will not make it through.

Prof C. is a great prof that's really passionate about her work. The concepts and readings are very dense and abstract, so she does her best to break things down and ensure understanding. That being said, SO MUCH READING. Sometimes 5+ hours per class. She can be a bit scattered and disorganized, but overall she has a good heart + good intentions!

Prof C is a little disorganized, but she was mostly OK. She definitely has a tendency to interrupt student led discussions, sometimes in an uncomfortable way. For a first-year seminar Pass/Fail class, it was just fine. You absolutely can't reach her outside of class - don't event try. The topic is an important one though and she's knowledgeable.

analysis.name: Carson Cistulli
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: carson cistulli. where do i start? if you have him as a teacher then consider yourself blessed by the schedule gods. his clothes alone are reason to come to class. never mind the fact that he's an awesome teacher. just wait until he wears "the bear" you'll know it when you see it.

Carson is on a mission to turn me into a lit scenester!  I would recommend him though; he gave me freedom to write fun and creative papers I normally wouldn't in a writing class.  He uses great sources and tries to expose students to good stuff like Brahms, Machiavelli, and Vonnegut (who would frown on my use of a semicolon).  Go for it!
Excellent sense of both tangibles and intangibles, his mind is like an irrepressible dirigible.
English 112 is not the most exciting subject but Carson always made the class fun!  He gives useful feedback on papers and this class was probably the most entertaining class i've had at Umass.

By far one of my favorite professors so far. He really made the class fun by giving us extra points for using cool words in our essays (fantabulous, mega fly, the bomb diggity) and by always being able to relate ANYTHING to sports. Such a great guy, personality kind of reminds me of Mo Rocca.

analysis.name: William Clement
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Probably one of the worst courses I have taken at Umass. The labs are very tedious and often have you doing mindless calculations for the sake of nothing. It's not particularly difficult but it is the worst class I have taken at Umass. It's no wonder the geology department recruits so hard with this intro class, it's easy to see its not any good.

I did not enjoy this class at all! Only took Dynamic Earth for a Gen. Ed. but it was super boring. He only has 4 Exams drops the lowest grade which is 90% of your grade, and a few assignments that require you to write two sentences worth 10% of your grade. The "textbook" was a Geology novel that I did not read but 1 or 2 Q's are on the exams fromit

This class is one of the worst classes I have taken so far. Labs are long and tedious and boring. The teacher in the lectures just talks a lot and the lectures are REALLY boring and that's the reason the lecture hall is always more than half empty. There are no study guides or anything before the exams either and a lot of homework.

I would really avoid taking any class with this professor at all cost. The lectures slide make absolutely no sense outside of the context of the lecture, this would be fine if he did not fly through the material and you could take notes at a reasonable pace (I write fast). The echo 360's have no sound which makes them useless. The test are ok.

Has a lot of boring assignments that are due each week but are easy and can be completed in less than 15 minutes a week. The lectures are boring so make sure to study the slides if you don't go to class. There are 4 tests but 1 drops and there is group portion. Lab is easy when you go to office hours so they can help you.

analysis.name: Justin Clarke

He was happy to answer questions and gave feedback to each student.

Justin Clarke was the TA for CS348 and is the best one I have had thus far. He is genuinely helpful on Piazza and easy to talk to. When the professor was busy, Justin was usually fast to respond on Piazza and took time to clarify any misconceptions people have during his office hours.

A great TA who's quite helpful in office hours, although it does take time for him to post stuff on Moodle. 348 is pretty laid-back and if you simply do the work and go to his office hours, you will do well.

analysis.name: Chris McDaniel

Very rude person. Doesn't help you if you are in trouble. He will make you feel you are damn stupid, and he doesn't care what you feel. Don't reply the e-mail which he thinks this problem he doesn't care. You'd better to deal with your TA more than him. If take this course, try not deal with him in person. I will piss you off.

Honestly the guy is very clearly a research professor and I frankly don't blame hime for making this class a pain. However good lord this is simple chemistry but you would think it's some kind of a divinchi code. He completely lacks any understanding whatsoever and just has absolutely no real social skills.
Chris McDaniel is probably the biggest sore loser when it comes to professors in the orgo field of the chemistry department.

Had him for the Gay Culture first year seminar. He was passionate about everything he taught. Radiates the most positive energy.

I took him for his English 131, outgoing and loud professor who is passionate about what he teaches. Class was fairly easy, but also he keeps it involved and its not dead in the classroom. 3 books, 3 essays. You can also skip class he takes attendance randomly.
RECOMMEND TAKING THIS CLASS. Tyler is a really nice professor, the materials are really interesting to learn

Very very very nice profesor. Take his first year seminar, way easier than everyone else's that I know. Very chill dude, you legit just have to show up. I think there was 2 assignments which were each 30 second presentations where you could stay in your seat.

analysis.name: Carey Clouse

Awesome professor, and I had a fantastic experience. Best 391A at Umass.  Discussion based seminar, great readings and only a interesting presentation is what you are responsible for. HIGHLY recommend.

Carey was such an amazing prof. She was super caring and considerate of what we could do after a year of virtual learning. I learned so much from her and my classmates from this class!

I esp liked folks reviewing my paper and the different things I would see. I think this professor could work on some things, but overall was decent, and I would take them again. I also took their poetry class and I appreciate the variety of diverse readers we read together in class!

I enjoyed this class because the assignments seemed fair and even though I wasn't a writing major. I learned a lot from the readings. I would take this course if it was more reading based than writing. This professor made me laugh and helped me ease into writing papers.

Cancelled at least 6 classes over the semester (almost always cancelled classes just before they were supposed to start) and late to the rest of classes (usually 10 minutes). This class is very heavy on class discussions and 'turning and talking.' Has been a very informative class.

analysis.name: CJ Llego
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: This was my favorite class last semester. CJ got us thinking about how to be happy in and out of his class; his class was engaging, fun and made me think about why we make the choices we make in our writings and lives. He's an open book and always made us laugh with his stories and helped me get a summer internship. Best professor at this school.

Great overall, he makes a hated first year class amazing and fun every lecture. There are only a few major essays which you really need to worry about and he exteneds if need be. Also his conferences tell you exactly what you need to do to get an A on the paper. The best thing about CJ is that he is more a peer than a prof.

I loved taking his class. There are a lot of essays but he broke is down in to smaller assignments and was helpful in conferences. He told funny stories to make the class more comfortable and connected them to my essays. Thank you for everything!
CJ helped me realize my true writing ability by allowing me the right amount of freedom and guidance. I owe him my continuing passion for the written word.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clark is dedicated to helping students learn and trying to give them skills that will actually benefit them in their future careers. Class was lectures on Mondays and group presentations on Wednesday. Large portion of the grade was made up of large case studies.

Great guy with lots of knowledge/connections in the industry. He is a great resource to go to for guidance. In Business In Society, the class typically consists of one group presentation per week, and he leaves his projects up to interpretation.

Class has 3 exams and that is your grade. Exams are no walk in the park so if your a bad test taker I wouldn't reccomend unless you are going into real estate. He is very knowledgeable about real estate but this class is not easy by any means, so only take it if you have an interest in real estate.
Great teacher, made going to an 8:30 class somewhat easy. Class is pretty test heavy but the material is not insanely difficult if you pay attention in class.

Professor Clark is very understanding and respectful, so never be afraid to ask him for guidance or support! He took the time to get to know everyone in class. He is an easy grader who mainly assigns group projects and some self reflections in between classes. Very easy class and easygoing professor.

analysis.name: Tim Cook
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I am not a STEM lover- I chose this class because I thought it would be a more applicable physical science credit but I was wrong. He has no passion and the class is really boring. Like I can't imagine a chemistry class being much better, so I'm not sure what better options non-STEM majors have, but at least all of the answers are online!

This is not an easy Gen Ed Physical Science credit for non-science people. If you are not a science oriented person, you will struggle. I do the work, go to class, and do not understand his lectures. Very stream of conscious lectures with incomprehensible graphs to follow. He randomly changed the grading percentages Week 11 of the course.
Tim is an overall nice guy who cares about the students and the course, but he is so boring. 1 homework assignment every week and 3 tests, so not too much work, but definitely boring. Easy gen ed.

Definitely don't take his class. It was his first time teaching which I am sure played some part, but he decided to change the way the class was graded (lowering everyone's grade) two weeks before the semester ends. When asked about the grade change, he basically said "I don't care, figure it out." Take any other class with any other professor.

Not an amazing professor but knowledgeable. Lectures are pretty boring. You get a double-sided cheat sheet that is super helpful. He is pretty shy but I felt like I got to know him & I like him much better now. People are saying they didn't learn anything but honestly I learned a lot & the material is soo important to know in the current world.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Cook
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I love Beth!!! She's the best. If you're struggling, go to her. She cares so so much and really wants everyone to be heard, and supported in their learning. I credit so much of my love for epi to her because she makes it so interesting and fun. My fav UMass prof.
the professor is nice, quite lecture heavy but interesting topics - feels like sphhs150 but with some challenge
Worst class I've ever taken. Expectations are not clear at all and she randomly crashes out on the class. Do not take her class ever.

This is the second course I have taken with Dr. Cook; she is an amazing professor. Lectures are clear and she is very kind about any sort of questions, both she and the TAs are very accessible out of class. Attendance is mandatory but I missed half and still got an A. SUPER EASY CLASS!

Love her as a prof! Such a slay. Very fair and caring! (always asking and implementing feedback). Graded based on participation (to get a perfect score u had to come to 20 classes), 3 exams, weekly moodle quizzes, and homework. There is extra credit and u can make cheat sheets for exams. Not an "easy" A but veryyy attainable + worthwhile if you try

analysis.name: N. C. Christopher Couch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: awful awful awful!!! did not show up for midterm, had us write 2 essays with no direction and gives 0 explanation of movies. He also leaves during screening and has no open dialogue with students or TA.

I took this class as a gen ed thinking it would be an easy A. I attended every class to take notes on everything he said (b/c there are no words on the PowerPoints-- just pictures of comics). Grading for the class consists of 2 exams, a 10 page paper, and class attendance. Avoid this class if you have no interest in comics and only need a gen ed.

If you can suffer through the dull lectures, you'll be rewarded with an easy A. Open note midterm and final, basically write your essay ahead of time and copy it into the test booklet. Two essays all year. Great choice in GenEd. Couch's speech impediment might drive you nuts though. Consider watching Breaking Bad during class to pass the time.

Interesting lecturer, very hands off. Only 3 grades all semester. I thought he was quite funny. Your grade is really TA roulette. Prof would give all As if he could, but my TA was a mess. Clearly very little guidance or structure given to TAs. Sometimes he takes attendance but usually forgets. Exams (essays) are handwritten but open note.

If you like reading comics/graphic novels you'll enjoy this class. He is knowledgeable and funny. Lectures are mandatory, sit at the front tho because he speaks quietly. Honestly, I never bought a single book and just found PDFs online. Midterm/final questions were given to us in advance and the exams were open-note.

analysis.name: Maria Correia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had Prof. Correia for Math 545 - Advanced linear algebra, and also some lectures of Calc 2(Math 132). She is one of my most awesome lecturers at UMass, though she has a very thick accent, you get used to it in 2-3 lectures, and it never hampers your understanding. She is very excited to teach, and you can literally see that in her lectures.

Her lectures are incredibly helpful. Missing a class is missing a concept because the lectures aren't recorded, but as long as you pay attention and follow along, it is incredibly helpful. It is clear that she cares about her students and will go out of her way to make sure that those who ask for help get the resources they need.

Professor Correia provides solid engaging lectures. The lectures are not recorded, however, notes are provided for each lecture which are very useful as they cover everything you need to know for the exams. She does have a slight accent, however she writes everything on the board. I enjoyed this course and would highly recommend!

Maria was an amazing professor (she's the course chair!). Her lecture slides are incredibly helpful, and the lectures are paced quite well. As long as you attend them and pay attention, you should do well. She was also more than happy to answer students' questions. The course also had a discussion section, which I didn't find too helpful.

Not understanding to student's circumstances. Rigid in policies with no extensions. Took in a summer session. One midterm and one final. 5 quizzes (MC through Webassig/Cengage and Open Response through Gradescope). Used honorlock extension for midterm and final. Final has multiple choice and open response questions. First time got this horrid grade

analysis.name: Connolly Ryan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Aside from the fact that his humor is stuck in high school and he tries too hard to be "relatable," his ideas on life are pretty complex and deep. I think his lectures get MAD boring by the end because the books you read in his class are all pretty much tied to the same idea. Not much room for discussion. Don't get him started on Hampshire College.

Loved this class! Just 3 papers along with weekly book reading. Had one pop quiz with various threats throughout the semester but none came to fruition. Overall an extremely easy class. Prof Connolly is zany and borderline morbid at times but he took a soul-sucking class and made it fun and engaging. 11/10 would recommend.

Chill and easy A, but I won't lie 201H with Professor Ryan is hugely overrated. You'll get plenty of feedback on papers, which helps grades if you put in effort. However, his Moodle page is basically empty and discussions often turn into long, dry monologues with not enough room for students to talk.

Just show up! You don't even have to talk and you could miss a couple of classes too. He let us out early sometimes. You really will learn a lot about BDIC too. If you an incoming freshman choose this as your seminar it's the easiest A ever!

Prof Ryan was one of my favorite professors. He's super passionate about what he teaches and jokes all the time. Every class is an open discussion consisting of 15% student participation and 85% monologue. Participation isn't mandatory but attendance is.
