read two extremely long "short" stories weekly w homework on both, essays take up 60 PERCENT of ur grade, she doesn't give out 100s, nearly impossible to end w an A. she is nice tho. but so much group work and attendance taken. way too much work just to fulfill literature requirement.

Nice woman but nothing is ever good enough for her. I am a very very good writer yet she always finds one minor thing to critique and almost never gives 100s. SO much reading with little time to do it. Lots of group work which I hate bc I hate talking to people

She was a great teacher and very caring towards her students. The essays make up 60% of your grade, but she was easy to reach outside of class and always gave helpful feedback on them. Class time is almost always spent discussing the reading as a class, which helps you with the essays when you're analyzing the text. Overall a fun/interesting class.

She was a really caring teacher and her class lectures never felt too awkward which can be hard for english gen eds. The three essays were moderately difficult but she provided lots of feedback on them and gave lots of opportunities to meet with her. Overall a great class with interesting readings and discussions.

analysis.name: Andrew Lan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Andrew is a new professor, the last two comments seem to be really trying to take a crack at him for making exams difficult, as this is supposed to be a difficult major. Andrew has a distinct teaching style, and though he could work on making the class more interactive, he does care for his students and is trying to learn how to be a better prof.

Uncompromising and stubborn. Course policies are super contrived and unintuitive. Most difficult part of class is trying to not get scammed by syllabus. He was an okay lecturer. He complained about having to teach the class once because he co-taught and had to teach the 'boring/easy half'. A bit unenthusiastic

Andrew Lan's section covers strictly more material than Parvini's. The midterm was also significantly harder than past semesters, making practice materials useless. Lectures are dry, and assignments are just PDFs/Canvas quizzes, leaving no room for error and forcing you to compare answers. The only highlights are his humor and a generous curve.

Decent professor. Rather dry lectures but made the exam super easy, so there is not much to complain about. I wouldn't take him as a professor again since he seems so unpassionate and unrelatable as a professor-- especially for a higher-level class. Ultimately, not a terrible professor if you have to take him but pick someone else if you can.

Course is difficult and you are told that at the start. Expect very minimal support to succeed in the class from Andrew and the TA's. How well you do in this class pretty much depends on your self-study skills, which is against the point of taking a class in general. Expect to feel unwelcome at office hours (which are 1 hour a week).

analysis.name: Andrew March
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Expect nightly reading, usually between 25–100 pages per week. Lectures are delivered without slides and consist of him speaking continuously. Has no problem calling you out for using your phone in a 200 person lecture. The grade is based only on 4 quizzes. He has a tick where he coughs or clears his throat during lectures which gets annoying.

He's definitely condescending and pretentious, but understandable bcs he is a very smart guy. Lectures can get hilarious with the examples he gives. Lectures with no slides, and will call you out in a 200 ppl lecture if he sees you using your phone. The readings every week were like 40-80 pgs depending on week. Only grades are 4 quizzes 20pts each

Andrew does the bare minimum with his effort to the class. He knows what he is speaking about however he doesn't know how to be an actual professor. He changed the final exam date so late that the TAs had to change their schedule. When I asked about it he just brushed it off like it didn't matter and decided to act like it was the student fault.

As of November 24th, he sent out an email, somehow forgetting that the FINAL exam was to be taken place on December 3rd instead of the eighth. Andrew does show his knowledge about the topics are good, but besides that, he does not know or care to be a professor. Doesn't even care enough to make lecture notes for in class. I took this for fun too.

Prof does not think its important to make lecture notes or slides at all. The most you will get from him is a brief summary of the philosophers covered in class, the only things that are graded are 4 in class exams and the discussion section. you will lose 10% every time you miss class. TAs could not care less to help out. TA or Prof doesnt care

analysis.name: Andrew Spracklen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Spracklen is a very kind person. He teaches in a very clear way and simply wants you to improve your writing skills. He requires you to meet with his twice throughout the semester to check in on two of your papers, which honestly helped a lot. He gives tons of feedback on your writing, which is daunting at first, but again very helpful.

This class has multiple projects which run throughout the semester. Doing good is based on the amount of effort put into the assignments. A great amount of feedback is given which makes redrafting and getting a better grade easier. Dr.Spracklen does check ins where you can discuss the feedback you got. A great section to pick for Jr. year writing.

Dr. Spracklen is an amazing professor. He is very invested in the growth and success of his students. He does multiple check ins with his students. The content is heavy and difficult but the class is set to go over the content multiple times. This class uses alternative grading which allows students to focus on learning instead of exam success.

Very kind professor in the biology department. Tackles a tough course material and explains it very well. Ddemonstrates that he is trying to do his best for his students by doing in-person check-ins to go over how the course is going for you specifically. Uses inclass assignments more as a way to review. By far one my favorite professors at UMass!

(Biology 580) Dr. Spracklen is such a nice guy. He tries his best to provide an engaging and comfortable environment to all his students. He is very understanding and flexible with deadlines. He is also sympathetic and is willing to help in any way. All you have to do is read the assigned portions, answer pre-lecture questions, and attend class.

analysis.name: Andrew Kitto
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, tough grader but very fair. Very responsive to emails and happy to help out.

Slides are chock-full of information and Kitto does read off of them, however it's all very clear and concise. He used to be an auditor but makes a great professor. Three exams, attendance mandatory, weekly homework's, frequently has extra credit opportunities. Super understanding when you email him about any issues too! I'd take him again.

Class sessions drown you in PowerPoint information, so reviewing for tests becomes difficult. Tests are often tricky and very specific, picking out details from one of many slides. Lots of group work, but graded fairly generously. A fairly easy class, just one that is hard to get through.

Great professor. Lectures are actually pretty interesting and important for the students as many will go into the auditing profession. Lots of slides but keeps you engaged with discussions. Really cool dude, put in the work and you will get a good grade

Course material is dry but professor Kitto makes it as interesting as possible. Tests are difficult and hard to study for. A lot of group work that is more generously graded. Professor Kitto is a good dude and cares about his students.

analysis.name: Andrew McGregor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very kind, helpful and easily accessible professor who teaches concepts super well. The course itself was the hardest I've taken and required a lot of effort and study on my end, however, the professor did a fantastic job accommodating my learning throughout the course.

Professor Mcgregor is an amazing lecturer. His lectures are very clear and thorough. He makes sure everyone understands the material well.  On Piazza, he answers everyone's questions. He really is awesome and understanding of the students.

I have a lot of respect for Andrew because he actually cares very much about his students. He goes out of his way to answer questions in great detail and ensures you understand. The material can be somewhat abstract, but I don't see how anyone else can give better lectures. He is also a great guy, and structured the course very well. Pretty easy A

Andrew is the best prof/person I have ever met. He listens to students, answers EVERY question with details. His class is very organized too. He posts all lecture slides and solution to every homework and exam (even practice exam). Don't hesitate to take his class or have a conversation with him about compsci or math! He's always there for you.

Nice guy, very helpful as a teacher, understanding. DON'T MISS CLASS! EVER! If you go to class and pay attention, you'll do relatively well. Course material is boring and it can be hard to focus in class on what's happening. Tests make or break the class for you. Homeworks: very long, don't procrastinate on these! TAs/Teacher are helpful.

analysis.name: Robert Dow
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 132 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Bob Dow is by far the only professor you don't want to end up with for 201H and I would say that you should wait for a different semester if he is your only option left when selecting classes.

Bob Dow is hands down the worst choice for a 201H professor. If you take his class, be ready for harsh vibes. Don't expect reasonable workload, don't expect flexibility, don't expect to be understood, heard, or respected. The papers (worth 80%) are impossible with draconian grading policies. 201H with Dow is nothing but an exercise in self-torture.

For a class that is supposed to be discussing "ideas", there isn't a whole lot of ideas being discussed besides his. Grading policy is impossible to figure out and gives little to no feedback on assignments. Frequently calls out students for not participating, not showing up on time, etc. in front of whole class. Makes class awkward.

Bob Dow is probably my least favorite professor at UMass. He's a very smart man who is generally respected and passionate about what he teaches, but he's a ridiculously hard grader, puts his students on the spot a lot, and doesn't give ample time to revise your papers. If you're late to class he'll call you out for it and hold grudges against you.

doesn't like to be disagreed with. will twist your words. makes students uncomfortable, so no one talks in class. will then get mad at you for not being 'brave.' seems like he's only teaching his opinions. probably a very good, nice guy, but the only good part of this class is the readings.

analysis.name: Andrew Farrar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Andy is the best professor I've ever had. He's not only a very funny and enjoyable lecturer who connects well with the class, but is also very efficient in his lecture material and facilitates useful discussions. He is straightfoward in his criteria and wants everyone to do well. Andy is love. Andy is life.

Andy is super personable and really tries to get to know his students and their interests. He will tailor lecture topics to student interests regularly. If you're trying to decide who to choose for CNS junior year writing, I really recommend him. He also schedules the class differently than the other professors, with less work around finals week.

Great guy, tries to be funny in class. Super interesting lectures and the exams are manageable. Dense information but definitely do-able. No homework! Only one group presentation. Overall fantastic class.

Andy meant well but was incredibly soft spoken and tried too hard to mix his humor into lecture content which became confusing. He often came off as rude and uncaring when contacted or approached with questions about the material. Wasted way too much time by calling attendance in our class, every single class, which had over 50 students in it.

Phenomenal professor, not only taught the most interesting class I've ever taken (Drugs and Behavior), but a very down to earth professor. The content in 535 is a bit dense, but he gives you every opportunity to succeed. Class is part lecture, part open discussion about fascinating aspects of pharmacology. Amazing class, amazing man, 10/10.

analysis.name: Sonja Drimmer
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sonja Drimmer is the best professor I've had a UMASS. She takes her lectures and makes them incredibly engaging. Her excitement for the subject is apparent and makes classes that much more enjoyable. To be sure however, this class was in no way easy. Major work needs to be put in, especially for the papers.

Drimmer's teaching style is utterly exhausting, I was criticized for a paper being "too well written" (I received a C), she did not respond to my email sharing I had a death in the family, and her grading felt subjective.  I had to attend a 5 hour lecture on rugs to get a decent grade with extra credit.  Still traumatized (in grad school now.)

One of the best professors I've ever had. She is the most interesting, funny, charismatic professor I have ever had. She is so cool and kind, and makes class genuinely enjoyable. She fosters engagement effortlessly, making the classroom laugh often and so many kids always raise their hands, which I have found is rare. 100000/10, highly recommend!

Professor Drimmer is super kind and so beyond passionate about what she teaches and what she knows. She makes lectures fun and engaging (as someone who's never taken an art class). She is always very well prepared for class and always is open to questions and comments about art or things outside of it. Only 3 exams and two papers

She's a really good lecturer, enthusiastic about the material she teaches. She emphasizes the important stuff and makes really helpful reviews and sheets to follow along with. Discussion assignments were graded really easy. If you show up and take notes you'll do good.

analysis.name: Peter  Dunn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Three papers, graded very easily. For two of them, I wrote a draft, edited it in under 30 minutes, and got above a 90%. Weekly homework for completion, very fun. Two weekly quizzes w/ 4 attempts. Final is an easy group project. Groups are assigned. Casual lecture style. Make sure to do all the little assignments, you can miss a few, but not many.

Not very difficult to get an A in this course, as there are no exams and the primary way to get points deducted is the essays, which he doesn't really give feedback on at all and also is pretty nitpicky about them, but it's fair. Lectures didn't feel engaging at all, but some of the topics were interesting. I'm an unrelated major, so maybe that's y

Lectures are kind of boring but oh well.  Regardless, he's an easily accessible professor, and the grading of assignments seems to be pretty lenient.  Just make sure to keep track of the graded online short quizzes and weekly activity assignments and you'll be fine.  There are 3 750-1000 word essays to be written but they were fairly doable.

I am really conflicted. This teacher is really nice and amazing but the content of the class is the most boring thing ever. The teacher is a little bit of a type A person but to the students benefit as the class is clearly structured. Despite him being a great person, the syllabus, slides, and lectures are painfully boring and uninteresting.

Peter is an advisor and head of the SustComm department. He's very interested in his students success and what he teaches. Only three shorter essays that were pretty easy to write. Helpful with course registration as well, if you can take this class and you are interested in SCD you should.

analysis.name: Lindsay  DuBois
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't buy the textbook. Those who bought it quit reading it after the third chapter. Attendance is mandatory but she is kind about students who come in late. I had the class split into two 1.5hr sessions at 8am. Professor DuBois LOVES politics, so you mostly talk about current events. It's a super easy class, interesting at times.

Such a boring professor. Attendance is mandatory and she gives you scuff for not coming in when she doesn't do anything educational during class. She goes off topic and on random tangents all the time. She doesn't have structure for the class and her grading system is so confusing and never aligns with what she says.

Don't buy the book. Her class is flipped and you are responsible for learning all of the info outside of class. The assignments are poorly outlined. Graded on exit tickets, 3 papers, 3 discussions, 1 presentation, 2 group projects, and final exam. She just yaps through the whole class.

Her final is beyond frustrating as it is "Lecture-Based"; however, our class is completely unstructured. She will put a couple of slides up with words and then go on tangents, of random stories and irrelevant conversations.

Overall extremely poor professor. Multiple quizzes based on textbook alone with no lecture component (Lecture after the quiz, not before; very unhelpful!). Lack of actual teaching, overload of irrelevant personal stories. Being difficult to reach outside of class on top of rude (and late) email replies makes Lindsey a poor fit for this role.

analysis.name: Joseph DuChene
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His exams closely resemble exam review slides and TA review worksheets. Even if you skip lectures, attend the last class before each exam. Homework is graded based on effort and completion. The slides are clear and easy to understand. He is approachable, passionate about the subject, and does a great job explaining concepts!

The course material can be made rigorous if one follows the textbook (Bard Electrochemical Methods) but this class was very easy, only going over rudimentary concepts. Some of our exam questions were taken straight from the practice problems. The class is fairly pleasant to listen in on.
Professor DuChene is kind, and quick to the point. The course material is fairly simple, but I would still advise showing up to lecture as his slides do not give much information on their own.

unfortunately, it seems as though Joe is a professor who does not care too much at all about teaching. it may be possible that the department forced him into the role. he's a great guy and the class is easy to do well in but i didn't actually learn anything or gain any value from quant lecture. i shouldn't get an A in a class while learn nothing.

Joe is a great guy, but I did not learn anything from his class. All the exams are recycled from previous years, and all hw can be found online so it is easy to do well, however you learn nothing. The lab is a completely different story- one of the worst labs ive taken here. Stay away from this class if you can.

analysis.name: Marco Duarte
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Throughout my journey in university, I have never came across such a class and professor. Homeworks will receive terrible grades, regardless if you do them in office hours with the TA's. Awful experience in this class, DO NOT take this class with Duarte. Its clear that he's just doing this for the money and does not have passion for teaching.

Genuinely one of the hardest classes for a subject that is seemingly very simple in concept. The way everything was organized was the worst I've seen by far in any course I've taken. You're more likely to hit the lotto than getting good feedback on everything. Watch out for exams, because there WILL be things that were never mentioned.

Absolutely TERRIBLE class, assignments are graded with pure inconsistency and professor shows no understanding of the students' situations. TA graders are absolute nightmares and when brought to the professors attention, he does not do anything. Does not reply to 90% of emails.

grading is incomprehensible and practically random. be prepared to do every assignment 2-3 times.

you learn nothing and the whole class is graded based on his random bs criteria, huge waste of time, take prof. leonard instead

This class is just bad and the professor does not care about his students succeeding. Homework directions can be vague but grading is overly harsh. Just skip taking this guy and take professor leonard, anyone but professor duarte!

analysis.name: Dwanna Robertson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Dee a while back. She was engaging and passionate about her work. However, she strikes me as a little self-centered, as she would only talk about indigenous people, and neglect other racial/ethnic minorities. She also rejected both myself and two others' LOR requests (too busy?) for grad school apps- again, somewhat selfish and unsupportive.

Dee was great! She may be a little intense about her ethnic background but she means well. She will tell it how it is and is very involved with her students. She will learn your name and who you are. Lots of easy writing and mostly free writes! Topics are inspiring and fun. Grades very fast with helpful comments and emails back quickly. Loved her!

Dee is a wonderful teacher! she really makes sense with her teaching...it is an easy a if you do all your work.  she even says its hard to fail this course.  she's very energetic and i looked forward coming to class even if it was 8am...i got an A! and it was so worth it. i highly recommend it! plus its 2 gen-eds
Dee is an awesome professor!She delves into issues that we see, but have never understood or knew they were they were there before. It's a great class!!

analysis.name: Rachael Dworsky
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is a Gen Ed for ALL students, yet Rachael grades as if each student is an English major. She is not understanding of attendance issues. It is extraordinarily difficult to predict what your final grade will be, as she uses a mixture of a check and number system, with no updates to where you stand.  Take this class with another teacher.

Rachael Dworsky is a sweet woman when she likes you, but definitely has a vicious side if you miss too many classes. Attendance is mandatory. I wasn't too crazy about her book selection but if you read you will do well. Pop quizzes, and a few essays. She gives you the option to choose the prompt you would like to answer in your essays. Fair class.

Worst class that I have taken. It appears as though she has difficulty understanding absences. She gives too much work and not enough time to complete the assignments, which is extremely annoying. Although she is not understanding...Rachael is a push over and you can easily by yourself more time, however.Good luck in not getting her angry.

TERRIBLE TEACHER! There is a lot of writing (to be expected), but it is complete and utter junk writing. She doesn't know what she is talking about and contradicts herself in her teaching. She has severe issues with her teaching style and does not seem to care if her students succeed at all. She is honestly the worst professor at umass.
this is by FAR with no doubt in my mind the worst teacher at all of umass. Take her class and then have the motivation to visit this website just to let people know.

analysis.name: Jacob Dyer-Spiegel
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Jacob is an incredible professor who, despite not being an engineer, has figured out ways to get us (Engin majors from all fields) to describe our mindset, process, lens, and vision for the future.The activities and prompts were so interesting that I wanted to put more time into my writing and communicating. He turned writing into engineering!

This was my favorite course at UMass. I loved the interactive nature of everything we did and Jacob's constant encouragement. I found I learned a lot about my own engineering process through the course and the way Jacob focused on practice. Excellent professor, highly recommend taking extra time to do all of the work fully & extra credits!

Jacob's awesome! As an engineering major, I despise writing. However, I genuinely looked forward to each class, knowing I would be in an interactive and engaging environment. He provides excellent feedback and is extremely supportive, eager to help clarify any points of confusion. If you need to take Engin 351, take it with Jacob!

Really nice guy. He cares a lot about students and will take an interest in pretty much all of the essay topics even with limited technical knowledge. I normally hate writing, but he really made the process as manageable as possible. He also provides really detailed feedback on all of the major assignments you submit.

You can tell Jacob loves teaching. He brings a huge energy to the class, builds from everyone's interests & viewpoints, and always makes himself available for clarifications, examples, and feedback. What I liked most is the way the assignments get you practicing writing skills while giving space to be creative with our engineering interests.

analysis.name: Dylan Ford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dylan is a cool guy, talks a lot interesting stuffs in the class. If you like to talk and share your opinion with him you can become great friends. The grade is tough to get, an A is extremely hard for me.  The best part is his lecture, easy-going, not boring at all and excited, he is funny. The worst part is the grade, again, hard to get an A.

He's a young, enthusiastic teacher who will not only make you interested in the topic, but make you laugh hysterically. Ive never quite had a teacher like Dylan before, depending on your own personality you may not like him. He's outspoken and doesn't censor anything which makes him unlike most professors and also much more interesting to work with

Dylan is the man, it's his first year teaching at UMass and he only teaches one class. He makes class funny and enthralling but actually gets his point across clearly. His assignments are not long and they really help with writing papers, which are not long at all. You can also choose to write about almost anything which makes writing fun.

If there is one teacher you should have for English Writing, it should be Dylan. He has given me an entirely new perspective on writing, and you can tell that he genuinely cares about his students. He allows you to express yourself in your essays, and he is always willing to help you. He's definitely the greatest teacher I have ever had.
A great guy who you can walk into class and talk about anything from popular movies to baseball to just about anything you ask him about. Very easy to work with and respects his students.

analysis.name: Brion Dulac
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Brion is definitely a pretty funny guy but seems a little off his rocker. I've probably written over 100 pages on papers for this class, he's big on written assignments. Pretty easy grader though all you have to do is talk every now and then in the class and actually do the assignments. He's a little weird and goes on tangents but he's a great guy

Brion is a great teacher, and en even better man. He is often scatter brained but has the best intentions. The perfect combination of smart, funny, and sweet. His Honors 291A uses a lot of movies and inspired me to start towards my film certificate. He sometimes brings in food. His stories are always interesting. He cares about his students.

I'm really glad I toke this seminar with Dulac.He's a pretty cool guy especially when analyzing movies.There's not much to say but just do all your work with some effort and you should get a good grade especially since he doesn't give that much work compared to other H291A professors.Loved all the movies we watched.

If you're looking for that movie-quality zany college professor, Brion is it. The semester started out very reading-heavy, but mellowed out immensely about halfway through. Brion is always engaging and it's clear that he cares about his students. I would definitely recommend taking this course with him.

Literally the best professor you will ever have. The homework is a ton, but very manageable if you email him for an extention. The papers he has you write are very reflective on yourself and on the topics in class. He is very caring and all-in-all the best person to meet in your life.
